## Facts (by id)

### a-bank-pinned-to-the-shipped-behaviour-is-pinned-to-a-moving-target
_A bank that measures "what the shipped path leaves undone" goes RED the day the shipped path does it — and every one of those reds reads as good news_

- **answers:** my probe bank went red after a behaviour change and the new numbers look better — is that a regression | a census dropped from 129/129 to 0/0 — did the problem go away | how do I write a bank whose subject survives the fix it is measuring | should a bank name the policy it measures, or just run the default command | why did a would_absorb=2 become would_absorb=0 after we shipped the absorption | how do I keep a before/after baseline once the after becomes the default | is a zero-check still a check after the thing it counted became non-zero on purpose | my bank pins a total that just changed for a good reason and there is no flag to reproduce the old one | should I re-pin the constant when a probe goes red after an intentional change
- **date:** 2026-08-14 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.17 slice 9 (the indirect-LR admission flip). `docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/guard_feasibility/probe.sh` went C1 `0/28 → 0/0`, C7 `129/129 → 0/0`, C8a `32 → 0`; `guard_dry_run/probe.sh` went D1 `2/0 → 0/0`, D13 `6 → 0`. Both were CORRECT extractions of an EMPTY population — the knots they census had been absorbed. Fixed by passing `--indirect-lr-admit-starvation-safe-only` at each report site, after which all 36 declared values are byte-identical to the pre-flip run.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/guard_feasibility/probe.sh && bash docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/guard_dry_run/probe.sh   # 18/18 and 18/18; every value unchanged across the flip because each names its admission`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-bank-pinned-to-the-shipped-behaviour-is-pinned-to-a-moving-target.md`](docs/knowledge/a-bank-pinned-to-the-shipped-behaviour-is-pinned-to-a-moving-target.md)

### a-bar-anchored-on-the-worst-healthy-case-can-be-met-by-degrading-it
_A bar anchored on the subject's worst healthy case can be met by degrading it — bound the anchor too_

- **answers:** how do I set a quality bar without inventing a number | my ratio bar passes, is that good | why did a bar that both subjects failed suddenly pass for one of them | what anchor should a performance ratio use | how can a self-derived threshold be gamed without anyone gaming it

### a-bootstrap-check-must-not-block-the-act-that-bootstraps-it
_Adding a new input to a baseline's identity block deadlocks the gate — the check fails because the row is missing, and the only operation that writes the row refuses to run while the check fails_

- **answers:** I added a field to my baseline and now nothing can regenerate the baseline | my gate refuses on a stale artifact and the rebaseline refuses because the gate refused | how do I widen a freshness/identity check without hand-editing the artifact it guards | should a rebaseline be allowed to ignore the failure it exists to resolve | my co-publication check covers a file that my own tool regenerates — is that safe | how do I tell an operator-declared adoption apart from a real breach
- **date:** 2026-08-16 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.21, TWICE, in two different slices of one leaf. Slice 1 made the instrument a fourth identity input of `PARSE-COST-RATCHET`'s baseline; the `instrument` row cannot exist until a rebaseline writes it, and the rebaseline was guarded by `if REBASELINE and not failures`, so identity divergence was a hard failure on EVERY path including the one whose purpose is to resolve it. Slice 4 hit the identical shape one surface over — `cost.md` is both a co-publication surface and an artifact the rebaseline REGENERATES, so its anchor could not be correct until the copy it was blocking had happened. Both fixed the same narrow way, and the second one was predicted by the first.`
- **reverify:** `grep -n 'REBASELINE' scripts/check_parse_cost_ratchet.sh   # identity_problem() and copublication_problem() both downgrade to a NOTE under PGEN_PARSE_COST_REBASELINE=1, and ONLY there; the ratchet's own breach check is untouched, so a rebaseline still refuses if a binding counter rose`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-bootstrap-check-must-not-block-the-act-that-bootstraps-it.md`](docs/knowledge/a-bootstrap-check-must-not-block-the-act-that-bootstraps-it.md)

### a-builtin-keyed-on-a-rule-name-shadows-a-real-definition
_A builtin that dispatches on a rule's NAME is a reserved word nobody declared — it silently shadows a grammar's own definition_

- **answers:** my rule is defined in the grammar but the stimuli generator emits nothing for it | a certificate probe shows parsed=false with an empty sample and the rule looks fine | why does the generator disagree with the parser about what a rule matches | is epsilon a reserved rule name in PGEN | where are the code generator's builtin rule names declared | how do I add a generator builtin without shadowing a grammar rule | the generator emits X:= with an empty right-hand side and the parser rejects it | a rule can never be witnessed but every spelling of it parses by hand
- **date:** 2026-08-22 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.16.3 (`PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0166`). `stimuli_generator.rs` matched `rule_name == "epsilon"` and returned `Ok(String::new())` before any grammar lookup, shadowing `grammars/ebnf.ebnf:324`'s real `epsilon := ("ε" | "epsilon" | "empty" | "λ")`. Codegen honours the definition — `epsilon` is NOT in `NATIVE_UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE_BUILTINS`. Every witness rendered `X:=` (empty rhs), which the parser rejects. Fix = gate on `!grammar_tree.contains_key("epsilon")`. Cert `144/0/111/33` → `144/0/112/32`; `spf` 8→4, 11→5, 7→3 at seeds 0/7/42.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline grammars/ebnf.ebnf --report-certificate-coverage --entry-rule grammar_file --count 40 --seed 0 | grep -o 'UNKNOWN=[0-9]*'   # 32, and PGEN_CERT_COVERAGE_DEBUG_PROBES=1 … | grep \"rule='epsilon'\" is now EMPTY`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-builtin-keyed-on-a-rule-name-shadows-a-real-definition.md`](docs/knowledge/a-builtin-keyed-on-a-rule-name-shadows-a-real-definition.md)

### a-cap-that-preserves-the-count-still-destroys-the-diagnosis

- **answers:** my report caps its findings list but publishes the true total — is that honest enough | a ratchet went RED and I cannot tell which new finding caused it | diffing two runs of my instrument returns no differences but the totals differ — why | should a diagnostic list have a cap at all, and what must come with it | how do I name the finding that pushed a count past its ceiling | when is the right move to fix the instrument instead of bisecting history

The report's `divergences` list is capped at 40 with `divergence_total` alongside, and the source comment reads *"the uncapped count travels alongside it, so truncation is always visible"*. A set-diff of the divergence lists from the ceiling's founding commit and from today came back EMPTY ON BOTH SIDES — the same first 40 rows, and the extra divergence past the cap. Nine grammar revisions were probed before the cap was recognised as the blocker; adding `PGEN_ENVELOPE_DUMP_ALL=1` (one edit) named the row on the first run - `use_clause_param_override_sv_only`, `arm1=semantic_annotation_inline` vs `arm2=semantic_annotation`. The repository had already paid this exact price once: `--lint-grammar`'s per-class cap of 40 hid 20 of SystemVerilog's 30 left-recursion findings until `PGEN_LINT_DUMP_ALL` existed.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/es13c2i_envelope_cap/probe.sh 2>&1 | tail -3   # A1 lists 40, A2 lists all, A3 x4 prove the counts do not move`

### a-certificate-delta-is-not-evidence-a-codegen-change-reached-the-shipped-parse
_The certificate observes the PROTOCOL graph — a cert delta does not prove a codegen change reached the parse a consumer runs_

- **answers:** my codegen change moved the certificate — does that prove the shipped parser changed | which graph does certificate_coverage actually parse on | why does bare_parse matter when I am measuring a grammar or codegen fix | the cert moved but a real parse behaves the same — which one is wrong | which oracle proves a change reached the fused cascade graph | does enable_coverage change how the parse executes | I fixed one codegen emission site — how do I know there are not others | why do all the counter dumps agree with each other and still miss the defect | how do I stop a decision from being spelled at several codegen sites
- **date:** 2026-08-23 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.16.4a (PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0177). The layout-skip decision was spelled SIX times across four modules; changing only `generate_atom_logic` (the PROTOCOL emitter) moved `ebnf` cert `144/0/112/32` → `144/0/113/31` at seeds 0/7/42, delta attributable by rule name, while a `bare_parse` production parse was untouched. `parse_harness_equivalence_gate` caught it — `ebnf DIVERGE samples=81 agree=60 diverge=8`, interpreter `"elements":[{"content":"   ","type":"whitespace"}]` vs oracle `"elements":[]`. Fixing three of six then made `cascade_match_*` and `cascade_build_*` disagree on `start_dynamic` and codegen emitted a parser that panicked on its own tape (`derivation-tape drift in rule 'whitespace': expected TokStart, found TokEnd(157319)`).`
- **reverify:** `make -C rust SHELL=/bin/bash parse_harness_equivalence_gate   # the ONLY standing oracle whose generated-parser side is a bare parse_full_*; 11/11 certified grammars byte-identical. Then: cargo test --features 'generated_parsers ebnf_dual_run' --lib layout_owning_terminal_tests   # pins the six callers of the one shared decision`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-certificate-delta-is-not-evidence-a-codegen-change-reached-the-shipped-parse.md`](docs/knowledge/a-certificate-delta-is-not-evidence-a-codegen-change-reached-the-shipped-parse.md)

### a-classifiers-residual-is-its-most-important-output
_A classifier's residual is its most important output — print it verbatim, cap it rather than zero it, and extend the rule by enumeration_

- **answers:** how do I classify a corpus field without over-fitting the rule | my classifier left half the population unclassified — is the result still valid | should a gate require zero unclassified rows | how do I extend a classification vocabulary safely | why did my regex classify tool testimony as a spec citation | is mentioning IEEE 1800-2017 the same as citing a clause | how do I publish a share or percentage over a corpus honestly | how do I stop a classifier from matching a task-leaf id as a clause number | what is the trust bound on the SV corpus answer key
- **date:** 2026-08-24 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `CORPUS-KEY-AUDIT.2 (PGEN-CORPUS-KEY-AUDIT-0004), classifying the provenance of all 10 090 keyed rows in the SV adjudication manifests. Cut 1 ('any basis naming IEEE 1800-2017 is clause-cited') classified all 623 Surelog rows — basis 'parses under Surelog's IEEE 1800-2017 grammar' — as spec citations; they are the purest tool testimony in the corpus. Cut 2 ('a clause cite needs an A.n.n production') then missed 72 rows citing a numbered clause directly. Both settled by enumerating the token after every edition mention: 623 'grammar' / 72 a dotted number / 63 'clauses|Annex|production', exhaustive over all 758. Separately, the first complete run left 4 961 rows (49 %) unclassified while printing a clean-looking table and a headline; enumerating those shapes took the residual to 4, all printed verbatim. Final: clause_cited=627 tool_testimony=2287 suite_convention=7172 unclassified=4.`
- **reverify:** `python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/corpus_key_audit/key_provenance_census.py   # rows=10090 ... unclassified=4; the artifact prints all four verbatim. python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/corpus_key_audit/key_provenance_census.py --self-test   # arms=16 failed=0, including both historical mistakes pinned in OPPOSITE directions and the negative arm proving a task-leaf id (.8b.3) is not read as a clause number. bash scripts/check_corpus_key_integrity.sh   # tier A4 caps the residual`

### a-comment-syntax-the-frontend-does-not-know-is-a-silent-language
_A comment syntax the frontend does not know is a silent language — implement the meta-grammar's comment rule, not one spelling of it, and diff the WHOLE envelope after a frontend change_

- **answers:** why did commented-out alternatives end up live in the generated parser | the meta-grammar allows // comments — does the EBNF frontend | why did a comment-only edit move the ebnf_raw_ast digest | how do I know a frontend fix changed only what I meant to change | cargo test --lib passed with 0 tests — is the module feature-gated

- **evidence:** `PGEN-EBNF-FRONTEND-SILENT-TRUNCATION-0002: grammars/ebnf.ebnf:583-586 defines `#` and `//` as line comments; rust/src/ebnf_frontend.rs knew `#`. 77 `//` lines in grammars/systemverilog.ebnf survived by being dropped or swallowed, and `parseable_source_item`'s three `//`-commented alternatives were LIVE in the released parser (each with an empty regex token), reachable via --entry-rule systemverilog_parseable_file. 14 return-annotation payloads in 11 rules carried the comment that followed them (return_scalar). Fix: comments cut from payloads, `//` a comment in all four frontend sites; one generated parser moved in one rule, ten byte-identical; SV release 1.0.205, ledger SV-0078.`

### a-conditional-compilation-gate-is-a-claim-about-which-trees-exist
_A `#[cfg]` gate keyed on ARTIFACT PRESENCE is a claim about which trees can exist — put it on the data, never on the accessor a feature-gated caller reaches_

- **answers:** my crate builds for me but a fresh clone dies with E0425 cannot find function | rustc says found an item that was configured out — how did this ever compile | the target that generates my artifact needs a build that needs the artifact | why did a build-flow one-liner with byte-identical outputs break the bootstrap | how do I test the cold-clone build configuration without deleting my generated files | how can a gate prove a fresh-clone build works when every dev tree is warm
- **date:** 2026-08-25 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `CI-PARITY-GATE-ROT.40. PGEN gates code on two independent axes — cargo FEATURES (caller-chosen) and `has_generated_*` ARTIFACT cfgs that `build.rs` sets from what is on disk. `parse_harness_equivalence` is gated on FEATURES and called `parser_registry::active_grammar_profile`, gated on ARTIFACTS. Every developer tree has a populated `generated/`, so it compiled everywhere for 10 days while a fresh clone died on one `error[E0425]` at the FIRST command README's Quick Start names. Fixed by DELETING the gate from the accessor (the artifact knowledge was already gated one level down, in a cfg'd match arm), not by adding a `cfg(not(...))` twin. Measured before 101 / after 0, then widened to every declared feature set — 9/9 arms.`
- **reverify:** `rust/scripts/cold_clone_build_probe.sh --census --self-test   # 9/9; the --self-test RED CONTROL re-injects the founding gate into an isolated copy and must reproduce the identical E0425`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-conditional-compilation-gate-is-a-claim-about-which-trees-exist.md`](docs/knowledge/a-conditional-compilation-gate-is-a-claim-about-which-trees-exist.md)

### a-conservation-control-cannot-catch-a-misassignment
_A control that checks a TOTAL cannot catch a defect that MOVES value between buckets — the sum is identical either way, so only an INDEPENDENT oracle sees it_

- **answers:** my instrument has a ground-truth control and it passes — is that enough | what kind of control should I put on a tool that attributes a total across categories | the totals add up but the per-category numbers look wrong — how do I tell | how do I validate a profiler / attribution / accounting script before publishing its numbers | I am auditing a published measurement and my re-derivation disagrees — which one is wrong | what is the cheapest control that would have caught this | why did my checksum-style control pass on a broken parser
- **date:** 2026-08-15 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.20 slice 4. A `/usr/bin/sample` attribution script carried the control `sum(self_time) == worker-thread root count`; it PASSED on all 8 reports while the script was silently ingesting `sample`'s second section (`Total number in stack (recursive counted multiple, when >=5)`, 694 lines) as call-graph rows, re-parenting **14 022** samples onto the last row of section 1. Headline effect — LR self-time read **18.12 %** instead of **2.27 %** (an **8×** error) and inclusive **39.52 %** instead of **23.67 %**. Caught by an EXTERNAL oracle: `sample`'s own `Sort by top of stack` per-symbol table, where **2 of 195** symbols disagreed, one with a self-time of **−14 015**.`
- **reverify:** `python3 -c \"import re,sys; sys.exit(0)\"   # the durable artefact is the control itself: docs/tasks/ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.md `.20` slice 4 records controls C1-C5, of which C4 (per-symbol agreement with sample's own table) is the one that fired and C2 (conservation) is the one that did not`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-conservation-control-cannot-catch-a-misassignment.md`](docs/knowledge/a-conservation-control-cannot-catch-a-misassignment.md)

### a-conservative-encoding-in-a-channel-that-cannot-express-the-fact-is-not-free
_When one field carries two kinds of fact, the one that does not fit gets encoded with the most conservative available value — and that encoding is a cost nobody prices_

- **answers:** one field carries verdicts from several sources and one of them has no natural value to write — what do I write | is it safe to widen a value to the most conservative option so the consumer stays correct | my cache went from fast to catastrophically slow after a soundness fix that measured clean — where do I look | a guard that is supposed to be a bound turned into an unbounded search — what class of bug is that | when is it right to split one taint channel into two | how do I know a taint scope is expressible in my cache key at all | a soundness fix was correct and measured — why did it still cost something enormous | should a resource-exhaustion verdict and a semantic verdict share a propagation path | how do I cache a failure whose validity depends on context the key does not carry
- **date:** 2026-08-21 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `PGEN `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.43`. `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.12` routed three recursion-guard verdicts through one field — a parse-stack FRAME INDEX. Two of them (`Infinite`, `LeftRecursive`) name a blocking frame. The whole-stack DEPTH CEILING names none, so it wrote `0`: the index outside every rule. `.3.12`'s gate refuses to cache a failure whose block came from a frame outside the memoized rule, so `0` made that true for EVERY rule at `entry_depth >= 2` and ONE ceiling trip disabled FAILURE memoisation for the rest of the parse. Measured on the shipped SystemVerilog parser: 315 nested parens 0.15 s accepted, 316 0.23 s, 317 4.90 s, 318 NO RESULT in 30 s. `.3.12` itself was correct, measured, and fixed real wrong-rejections; the `0` was the unpriced half.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/deep_nesting_cliff/measure_cliff.sh 60   # SV rejects past ~320 in bounded time; before the split it returned nothing at 318`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-conservative-encoding-in-a-channel-that-cannot-express-the-fact-is-not-free.md`](docs/knowledge/a-conservative-encoding-in-a-channel-that-cannot-express-the-fact-is-not-free.md)

### a-control-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-control
_A two-arm control is worthless unless the arm you changed is an input the instrument actually reads — stash the source, and an instrument that reads a generated artifact gives you the same run twice_

- **answers:** I stashed my change and the two arms came back identical — does that prove my change is innocent | how do I know a before/after control actually controlled for anything | a gate went red right after my commit and git stash says it is not mine — can I trust that | why did reverting my grammar edit not change the tool's output at all | what makes a control valid rather than just two runs | how do I tell whether an instrument reads my source file or a generated copy of it | my two arms agree and I want to publish that the regression is pre-existing | is a byte-identical diff between arms evidence, or the absence of evidence
- **date:** 2026-08-22 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.17.1 (PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0161). `ebnf_frontend_dual_run_gate` went RED on `systemverilog` (envelope `155 > ceiling 151`) in the same session as a `grammars/ebnf.ebnf` repair. `git stash`-ing the grammar and re-running `ebnf_dual_run_diff` returned byte-identical 155-row divergence sets — an apparent exoneration. It was a no-op: `rust/src/bin/ebnf_dual_run_diff.rs:13` `include!`s `env!(\"PGEN_EBNF_PARSER_PATH_RESOLVED_BIN\")`, which `rust/build.rs:101` resolves to `generated/ebnf.rs`, so arm 2 never reads `grammars/ebnf.ebnf`. Proven by removing the file: rustc reports the env var undefined at `:13` plus `error[E0432]`. The valid control rebuilt `generated/ebnf.rs` from the pre-fix grammar (sha `3028814854e0…`) and the differ with it; it also returned 155, so the conclusion survived — but the first argument for it was void.`
- **reverify:** `mv generated/ebnf.rs /tmp/ && (cd rust && cargo build --features ebnf_dual_run --bin ebnf_dual_run_diff); mv /tmp/ebnf.rs generated/   # rustc names the dependency: `environment variable PGEN_EBNF_PARSER_PATH_RESOLVED_BIN not defined` at ebnf_dual_run_diff.rs:13 + error[E0432]. Then, for the no-op itself: git stash push grammars/ebnf.ebnf && shasum -a 256 generated/ebnf.rs && git stash pop   # sha UNCHANGED by the stash => the arm never moved. NB grepping the .rs for `include!` shows only env!(...) — the path lives in rust/build.rs:101, which is exactly why the trap is hard to see.`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-control-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-control.md`](docs/knowledge/a-control-that-cannot-fail-is-not-a-control.md)

### a-control-that-names-its-subject-by-revision-expires
_A RED control that identifies its subject by REVISION expires the moment the fix lands — identify it by the PROPERTY that makes it the subject, and it keeps working forever_

- **answers:** how do I write a RED control that proves my guard changed something | my before/after control uses HEAD~1 — is that safe once I commit | how do I prove a refusal is the guard and not just that nothing was going to happen | how should a probe fetch the pre-fix version of the code it is testing | why did my adversarial arm start passing vacuously after the fix landed | what makes a control durable rather than true-on-the-day
- **date:** 2026-08-17 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2f(d). A guard was added to `tools/extract_systemverilog_lrm_profiles.py` so it refuses to overwrite an output it did not reproduce. Ten green refusal arms proved nothing on their own — each is equally consistent with *the guard works* and *nothing was going to be written here*. The RED arm runs the PREVIOUS revision of the tool at the same copy of the deliverable and measures `rc=0` with return annotations `2292 -> 0`, i.e. a silent destruction of the AST contract. The first draft fetched that revision with `git show HEAD~1:<tool>`; the moment the guard is committed, HEAD carries the guard, `HEAD~1` drifts to an unrelated commit, and the arm would test the guarded version and pass vacuously. Rewritten to walk `git rev-list -n 40 HEAD -- <tool>` and take the first revision whose source does NOT contain the refusal string — probe `EXTRACTOR-GUARD 14/14`, arm A13 reporting the revision it selected.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/es13c2f4d_extractor_guard/probe.sh 2>&1 | tail -3   # A13 must name a revision, A14 must go RED`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-control-that-names-its-subject-by-revision-expires.md`](docs/knowledge/a-control-that-names-its-subject-by-revision-expires.md)

### a-control-validates-the-property-it-is-built-from
_A control validates the property it is built from — a NEW property needs a new argument, never the old control run again_

- **answers:** my instrument has a control and it passes — is the new conclusion covered by it | I added a question to an existing instrument, do I need a new control | the control is green but the answer feels wrong — what can a control not see | is a passing control evidence that the ordering/succession logic is right | how do I tell whether my control is blind to the thing I just started measuring | I am comparing two counters — are they even on the same clock | why did my cross-check pass while the derived verdict was nonsense | when is it safe to reuse an instrument's existing control for a new claim
- **date:** 2026-08-29 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.67(c)(iii) (PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0131). The allocation LIFETIME tape in rust/src/bin/parse_alloc_census_probe.rs stamped allocations with ALLOC_CALLS and releases with FREE_CALLS — two counters that count different events — so every succession verdict (alloc(A) < alloc(B) < free(A)) compared incomparable numbers. Its control, `live at instant I`, reconstructs the size-class table at the snapshot instant and passed with 148 of 148 (input, class) pairs matching byte-for-byte, BOTH before and after the defect was fixed: that comparison puts alloc ordinals against I's alloc ordinal and free ordinals against I's free ordinal, staying inside one clock each time. Fixed with a single EVENT_SEQ that every allocation AND every release advances.`
- **reverify:** `python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/eus67c/rehash_spike_report.py docs/tasks/artifacts/eus67c/rehash_tape.tsv docs/tasks/artifacts/eus67c/rehash_meta.tsv docs/tasks/artifacts/eus67c/rehash_classes.tsv | head -3   # '148 (input, class) pairs ... 0 mismatched'. This re-derives the control and shows its SCOPE is residency-at-an-instant; it does NOT replay the two-clock form, which was never committed (see the honest limit below).`

### a-counter-that-cannot-tell-a-cache-hit-from-work-prices-them-alike
_A counter that cannot tell a CACHE HIT from real work prices them alike — so a "regression" it reports may be pure cache traffic, and the gate that reads it needs a typed way to say so_

- **answers:** my deterministic perf counter rose but I don't think anything got slower — how do I tell | how do I prove a cost rise is memoization lookups rather than new work | my perf gate refuses every rise and my fix is correct — what is the sanctioned way out | how do I let a gate accept a measured regression without turning it into a waiver | what makes an exception record different from a rubber stamp | should a cost baseline ever move upward, and what has to be true first
- **date:** 2026-08-18 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2j + ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.36 (2026-08-18). Restoring an IEEE 1800 A.8.4 branch the SV grammar had lost raised PARSE-COST-RATCHET's binding counters: entries 416,424,205 -> 417,009,457 (+0.14 %) and memo_hits 186,926,969 -> 187,512,221 (+0.31 %). The two deltas are IDENTICAL to the unit (+585,252 each) and `committed` is FLAT at 7,123,491. ⭐ RE-DERIVED PER FILE under director challenge (`-0231`): of the 192 pinned sample files, 149 moved and ALL 149 satisfy delta_entries == delta_memo_hits AND delta_committed == 0 individually, with zero accept-verdict flips -- so it is not an aggregate coincidence. What that measures exactly is that the number of NON-memoized entries is unchanged on every file; the entire rise is memo-neutral. The counter cannot see that: a memo hit is one rule entry, exactly like a parse. ⛔ The gate's breach text already said 'record it as irreducible with the measurement that proves it' and there was nowhere to record it -- every rise was a fail() and the rebaseline refuses while a failure stands, leaving, for a rise that elimination does not remove, abandon-the-fix or skip-a-doctrine. (The gate's FIRST branch, eliminate, was genuinely exercised: two of three widened sites were dropped and two-thirds of the rise went with them.)`
- **reverify:** `PGEN_PARSE_COST_REMEASURE=1 bash scripts/check_parse_cost_ratchet.sh   # a rise is accepted only by a docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/parse_cost_ratchet/accepted_rises.tsv row naming the EXACT from/to plus a coded invariant, which the gate RE-EVALUATES on the run's own numbers; four refusal arms plus a control are bash docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/accepted_rise_gate/probe.sh`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-counter-that-cannot-tell-a-cache-hit-from-work-prices-them-alike.md`](docs/knowledge/a-counter-that-cannot-tell-a-cache-hit-from-work-prices-them-alike.md)

### a-coverage-report-cannot-see-a-production-the-grammar-never-declares
_Coverage measures reach over the DECLARED rule set, so a construct the grammar never spells is invisible to it — a missing rule cannot be UNKNOWN, only absent_

- **answers:** my certificate/coverage report is clean — does that mean the grammar is right | what class of grammar defect can coverage instruments never report | two coverage instruments agree — how much confidence does that buy me | the residual UNKNOWN list is adjudicated benign — is there anything left to do | should I rebaseline a red gate once every number checks out | where do I look when a keyword is rejected but no rule is missing from the report
- **date:** 2026-08-20 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2x(a) (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0259`). Adjudicating `sv_cert_recognized_union_gate`'s 53 residual union `UNKNOWN`s found all 53 benign — 43 LR-eliminator-synthesised `property_expr_lr_*` rules (independently `GAP` 0-of-184-files in `stimuli/sv/characterization/rule_coverage_sv_2017.tsv`) and 10 witness-planner reach gaps whose constructs each PARSED. Reading `prop_primary_sv_2017` to explain the 10 found `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf:6666` — `implies := trivia \"->\"`, a token rule named after an IEEE 1800 keyword — so `a implies b` (A.2.10, and `implies` is reserved per Annex B) is REJECTED while `-> b` and `a |= b` are ACCEPTED though no IEEE 1800 production reaches either. (A third probe, `a -> b`, was first classified as over-acceptance and corrected: §11.3.2 makes implication `->` a binary EXPRESSION operator, so that one is legal and serves as a control.) There is no `kw_implies_*` anywhere, so the missing production has no rule, hence no row, in either instrument.`
- **reverify:** `printf 'kw_implies in the SV grammar: %s\\nrows naming it in the corpus coverage TSV: %s\\nwhat the rule called implies actually is: %s\\n' \"$(grep -c kw_implies grammars/systemverilog.ebnf)\" \"$(grep -c kw_implies stimuli/sv/characterization/rule_coverage_sv_2017.tsv)\" \"$(grep -m1 '^implies :=' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf)\"`

- **answers:** why are files that can never parse sitting in the DARK worklist | how should a corpus census treat a file that is not source text at all | should I remove non-source files from the denominator or leave them counted | what happens when an answer key says must_accept on a memory image | how do I stop a new hex image or command-line file from landing silently in a parse census

A byte detector (`not_source_text()`, three stated shapes) moved exactly 350 rows into `deferred:not_source_text` — DARK 4 363 → 4 013, zero verdicts moved, zero adjudicated rows hit over all 16 336 files.`

### a-derived-block-publishes-the-first-reason-it-recognises-so-the-assertion-must-be-derivable-from-the-tracked-tree
_A derived block publishes the first reason it recognises — when a leg's real verdict rests on an untracked artifact, declare the assertion's derivation from the tracked tree, or the book publishes the weaker line beside it for as long as nobody looks_

- **answers:** why did the SystemVerilog book say leg 3 rests on a triage gate when a conformance gate existed | how does the done-bar audit judge leg 3 in the tracked-only reading the books publish | what is tracked_assertion_command in the done-bar register's leg3_surface | a reason table picks the first matching line — what happens when an audit prints two gates for one leg | why does the audit read a gate's artifact under its invoker's work directory | the family-status block for SystemVerilog leg 3 — where does its sentence come from
- **date:** 2026-10-08 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `DONE-BAR.3c (`PGEN-DONE-BAR-0028`). The SystemVerilog book's status block read *\"the only gate reading the external corpus is a TRIAGE gate\"* from 2026-09-03 — the day `sv_external_corpus_conformance_gate` landed (DONE-BAR.3b) — to 2026-10-08. The block is derived TRACKED-ONLY (the audit with its artifact root pointed at an empty directory), so the conformance gate's line read *no artifact — UNPROVEN*, and `report_family_status.sh`'s reason table, scanned in its own order, recognised the triage sibling's ⛔ line first. FAMILY-STATUS-CURRENCY held the page equal to that derivation on every commit: the sentence was current and wrong. The assertion the book should have published — `full_pass`: every row adjudicated, zero unexplained divergences — is a function of the tracked adjudication manifest alone (`corpus_conformance_compare.py --assert-tracked` → `rows=16336 adjudicated=7485 no_verdict=6245 unexplained=0 full_pass=false`). The register now declares that derivation (`tracked_assertion_command`), the audit evaluates the same `pass_query` over it when no artifact exists (controls C8), a triage gate beside a conformance gate prints an informational line rather than a ⛔ (C9), and the audit also reads an invoked gate's artifact under its invokers' work directories (C10) — leg 1 had been reading a July copy under the SOTA aggregate while the formal umbrella held a seven-hour-old one.`
- **reverify:** `bash scripts/report_family_status.sh systemverilog --markdown | grep '3 — external' (expect the CONFORMANCE gate's own assertion, not the TRIAGE sentence); bash scripts/report_family_status.sh vhdl --markdown | grep '3 — external' (expect the TRIAGE sentence — VHDL has no conformance gate); python3 stimuli/sv/corpus_conformance_compare.py --assert-tracked stimuli/sv/characterization/adjudication_manifest.tsv | jq .full_pass; bash scripts/audit_done_bar.sh | grep 'controls reproduced' (expect ≥ 24)`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-derived-block-publishes-the-first-reason-it-recognises-so-the-assertion-must-be-derivable-from-the-tracked-tree.md`](docs/knowledge/a-derived-block-publishes-the-first-reason-it-recognises-so-the-assertion-must-be-derivable-from-the-tracked-tree.md)

### a-determinism-check-over-a-re-read-input-must-pin-the-input
_A determinism check that re-reads a mutable input once per iteration must record WHICH input it read — otherwise its failure message cannot tell "the tool is nondeterministic" from "the file changed under me", and the two send you to opposite places_

- **answers:** my gate says 'signature drift vs seed 0' — is the tool nondeterministic? | how do I prove a rule count is deterministic rather than assuming it | what does a cross-seed determinism check actually prove | why did a count differ between seeds when the code that computes it takes no seed | how do I de-confound seed from process when each seed runs in its own process | what identity does a multi-iteration gate need beyond its output signature
- **date:** 2026-08-20 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2x.1 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0255). sv_cert_recognized_union_gate read canonical total=1434 at seed 0 and 1433 at seeds 7/42 on the SV-0065 arm, and its determinism check fired. certificate_coverage() is PURE and its total is grammar.rule_order.len(), so no witness-search seed can move it — which made the observation look like nondeterministic rule SYNTHESIS and put every rule-count baseline in the repository in doubt. The discriminating probe (3 processes at one fixed seed, then one process per seed) measured 1434 six times out of six on the arm and 1433 three times out of three at HEAD, refuting BOTH recorded hypotheses. The gate re-reads $GRAMMAR_FILE once per seed (:255) and its signature (:307) is ten OUTPUT fields with no input identity; its only identity call (:177) is hoisted out of the loop and checks the contract, not the grammar. The gate's own arithmetic agrees: unmet=29 on the arm vs 27 at HEAD, where 27 is nine criteria on each of three seeds, so the +2 is exactly the two drift entries the loop appends. Census over the repo: 5 gates assert determinism across re-reads and 5 of 5 record no input identity inside the comparison loop.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/cert_count_determinism/gate_input_pin_census.sh   # GATE-INPUT-PIN-CENSUS: asserts_determinism=5 blind_to_input_change=4 (was 5 of 5; the SV cert gate was fixed by PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0258, the remaining four are ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.41). The attribution helper is proven by docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/cert_count_determinism/attribution_probe.sh -> ATTRIBUTION-PROBE: passed=20 failed=0`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-determinism-check-over-a-re-read-input-must-pin-the-input.md`](docs/knowledge/a-determinism-check-over-a-re-read-input-must-pin-the-input.md)

### a-deterministic-counter-cannot-see-a-per-entry-cost-rise
_A counter counts EVENTS, so a cost that moved PER event is invisible to it — but that blind spot is a PROPERTY of the metric, and the moment you put a NUMBER on it you have made a claim that needs measuring like any other_

- **answers:** should my performance ratchet key on wall clock or on a deterministic counter | my counter-based gate is green but the thing got measurably slower — how | how do I build a perf ratchet that survives a different machine or a hosted runner | a wall-clock baseline gave me the wrong regression number — what do I replace it with | is a deterministic oracle always better than a noisy direct measurement | how sensitive is my proxy metric to the regression I care about, actually | what do I write down when the only machine-independent metric is a weak proxy
- **date:** 2026-08-15 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.20 slice 1, corrected by .21, thesis RE-DERIVED by .26 (2026-08-16). PGEN specified a parse-cost ratchet on exact rule-ENTRY counters and published a numeric bound on their insensitivity — *"at least ~8.9x less sensitive than wall clock"* — derived as **+24.3 % wall clock / 2.741 % family share**. ⛔ BOTH terms were wrong. The numerator is REFUTED (.20 slice 5): not reproducible from the raw data of the runs that produced it, 7 estimator x era combinations giving ARM2/ARM1 in [0.9909, 1.0433], mechanism a fixed-arm-order artifact. The denominator was the wrong QUANTITY independently of that: sensitivity is how much the counter MOVED, not how large the rule family is — and the tracked A/B in the same leaf measures the move at **812 963 769 -> 899 064 022 entries = +10.59 %**, 3.49x LARGER than the family's own 24 644 435 entries. The counters SAW that change plainly. ⇒ the bound is retired, not re-computed (0.41x on the point estimate, 1.82x on the most adversarial pairing, and no admissible wall-clock figure survives). What stands is the STRUCTURAL limit, which needs no number.`
- **reverify:** `bash scripts/check_parse_cost_ratchet.sh   # OK — its every-run tier re-hashes the four inputs the 2.743 % share is a function of against docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/parse_cost_ratchet/family_share.json, re-checks that artifact's raw counts against the share it declares, AND holds this card's `Live LR-family share` anchor equal to it (ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.21 (f), .26); re-derive with `make -C rust SHELL=/bin/bash sv_parse_cost_family_share` (~70 s)`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-deterministic-counter-cannot-see-a-per-entry-cost-rise.md`](docs/knowledge/a-deterministic-counter-cannot-see-a-per-entry-cost-rise.md)

### a-fallback-arm-goes-inside-the-shared-rule-as-an-ordered-last-alternative
_A fallback arm goes INSIDE the shared rule as an ordered last alternative — a passthrough twin under longest_match pays the fallback at every site, including where the known arm already won_

- **answers:** where do I put an escape / fallback alternative for a rule that is referenced from many sites | why was the class_scope_escapable passthrough twin refused by the parse-cost ratchet | why is class_scope @branch_policy: ordered since 1.0.243 and why does class_scope_plain exist | does a passthrough dispatcher `a := b -> $1 | c -> $1` under longest_match derive both alternatives | when is an ordered choice provably the same choice longest_match would have made | why did the import-gate-first arm cost more than the ungated escape | how do I classify a shared rule's call sites into those that can afford an escape and those that cannot
- **date:** 2026-09-23 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.31 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0412, release 1.0.243): three spellings of ONE accept set measured by the parse-cost ratchet on the pinned 192-file sample — the passthrough twin `class_scope_escapable := class_scope -> $1 | wildcard_escape_class_scope -> $1` at nineteen sites under longest_match, entries +1.43 % (the dispatcher entered 3.6 M times, the escape's asks paid at every class_scope evaluation); the escape as class_scope's own LAST alternative under `@branch_policy: ordered`, entries +1.27 % (tried only where the known arm fails); the ordered escape opened with the zero-width `wildcard_import_open_gate`, entries +1.82 % (the gate and its `&( trivia )` lookahead entered 1.3 M / 0.9 M times, and a store-first arm re-asked the call prefix's known heads — the .27 memo-taint class). Every correctness lane (pins, three corpus lanes, AST identity sweeps, two-sided reading) read the three spellings identically; only the ratchet told them apart. docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md `.31`, rust/target/s375/prereg.md ADDENDA 5/8/10 (session scratch), grammars/systemverilog.ebnf `class_scope` / `class_scope_plain` / `class_scoped_call_prefix`.`
- **reverify:** `grep -n -B2 -A6 '^class_scope := ' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf | grep -E 'branch_policy: ordered|wildcard_escape_class_scope_type scope_resolution'   # two lines: the ordered policy and the escape as the LAST alternative; then grep -c 'class_scope_plain' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf   # 6 lines: the definition, the four type-position references, one comment`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-fallback-arm-goes-inside-the-shared-rule-as-an-ordered-last-alternative.md`](docs/knowledge/a-fallback-arm-goes-inside-the-shared-rule-as-an-ordered-last-alternative.md)

### a-gate-that-re-derives-a-population-must-read-which-producer-made-it
_A gate that re-derives its producer's population must read WHICH producer made it — and the member where the wrong method happens to agree is the one that makes it look correct_

- **answers:** my freshness gate re-counts a corpus and disagrees with the report — which side is wrong | how do I wire a second lane of the same family to a census gate | a denominator arm breaches on some sub-corpora and not others — is that a real drift | should a gate hard-code how a population is collected, or read it from a declaration | one of my controls agrees with the instrument — is that evidence the instrument is right | how do I know a green arm is measuring anything at all | what does it mean when a check passes on one member of a population and fails on the rest
- **date:** 2026-09-02 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13m / PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0332. `CORPUS-CENSUS-CURRENCY` arm (4) re-counted every declared sub-corpus by WALKING the tree, because the two lanes it had ever been pointed at were collected with `find`. ### a-git-pathspec-glob-crosses-directory-boundaries
_`git ls-files 'docs/tasks/*.md'` is not the shell's `docs/tasks/*.md` — a git pathspec `*` matches `/` too, so a census silently sweeps in every subdirectory_

- **answers:** why does git ls-files with a glob return more files than the shell glob | my file census counts twice as many files as the directory holds — why | does a git pathspec asterisk match a slash | how do I list only the files directly inside a tracked directory | my population size changed when I moved from ls to git ls-files | how do I size a corpus before adjudicating it
- **date:** 2026-08-30 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `DONE-BAR-VISIBILITY.2 (PGEN-DONE-BAR-VISIBILITY-0004). Sizing the task-tree population for a closed two-sided attribution register, `git ls-files 'docs/tasks/*.md' | wc -l` returned 337. The directory holds 164 top-level `.md` files; the other 173 live under `docs/tasks/artifacts/`, which the pattern was written to exclude. The error is silent and inflates in the direction that looks thorough — a 2x larger population to adjudicate, most of it machine-generated evidence files that are not task trees at all. Caught only because a second count, derived by filtering on the path's slash depth, disagreed.`
- **reverify:** `git ls-files 'docs/tasks/*.md' | wc -l; git ls-files 'docs/tasks/*.md' | awk -F/ 'NF==3' | wc -l   # the two numbers differ; the second is the top-level population`

### a-green-gate-over-a-generated-corpus-is-a-claim-about-the-corpus
_A green gate over a GENERATED corpus is a claim about the corpus — add the discriminating row first and require it to go RED_

- **answers:** my differential gate is green but I suspect a divergence — how do I tell | how do I verify a fix when the gate already passes before I start | should I add the test before or after the fix | a certified byte-identity claim has a bug in it — how did the gate miss it | what does a green generated-corpus gate actually prove | how do I stop a corpus gap from reading as a proof | my stimuli generator never produces the shape that breaks my code | how do I prove my new test case is discriminating and not just passing | is it enough to add a regression test after fixing the bug
- **date:** 2026-08-23 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.22 (PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0179). `return_annotation` sat in `parse_harness_equivalence_gate`'s CERTIFIED list — interpreter byte-identical to the generated parser — while carrying a live divergence: the parser emits `match_regex("[^']*", false)` ×5 and the interpreter passed `true`, so on `-> {k: ' abc'}` the parser captured `" abc"` and the interpreter `"abc"`. The discriminator is a quoted string whose CONTENT starts with layout, and the bounded stimuli generator never emitted one in 89 samples. Adding the rows to `CURATED_CORPUS` with NO code change turned the standing green claim RED (`DIVERGE samples=89 agree=80 diverge=8`); the fix then returned it to `4/4 ok`.`
- **reverify:** `Add the discriminating input to the gate's corpus and run the gate BEFORE touching any code — it must FAIL. make -C rust SHELL=/bin/bash parse_harness_equivalence_gate. Then fix, and it must pass. If step 1 does not go red, your row is not discriminating and the fix that follows is unverified.`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-green-gate-over-a-generated-corpus-is-a-claim-about-the-corpus.md`](docs/knowledge/a-green-gate-over-a-generated-corpus-is-a-claim-about-the-corpus.md)

### a-guard-after-a-greedy-regex-atom-cannot-shorten-the-match
_A guard placed after a greedy regex terminal filters where the match ENDED — it is not a lever on where it ends, so a terminal that matches too much must be constrained INSIDE the terminal_

- **answers:** my terminal is eating the delimiter that should follow it, how do I stop it | can I add a negative lookahead after a regex terminal to stop it over-matching | does a !(...) guard make a regex backtrack to a shorter match | how do I stop a URL or path terminal swallowing a closing bracket | my lookahead guard made the grammar worse, why | where should the constraint live when a terminal is too greedy | how do I let a delimiter appear inside an unquoted literal

- **evidence:** `|`
- **reverify:** `python3 -c \"import pathlib; s=pathlib.Path('grammars/semantic_annotation.ebnf').read_text(); a=r'url_reference := /(https?|ftp|file):\\\\/\\\\/([^\\\\s,\\\\]\\\\}\\\\)>\\\\\\\\]|\\\\\\\\.)*([^\\\\s,\\\\]\\\\}\\\\)>=\\\\\\\\]|\\\\\\\\.)/'; assert s.count(a)==1, 'anchor moved — re-derive the arm by hand'; pathlib.Path('rust/target/kmv_guard.ebnf').write_text(s.replace(a, r'url_reference := /(https?|ftp|file):\\\\/\\\\/[^\\\\s,\\\\]\\\\}\\\\)]+/ !(/\\\\s*/ \\\"=>\\\")'))\" && for i in 'http://PYJ=>http://aFC' '{ http://PYJ => http://aFC }'; do printf '%s' \"$i\" > rust/target/kmv_g.txt; ./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline rust/target/kmv_guard.ebnf --interpret-parse rust/target/kmv_g.txt --interpret-entry-rule annotation_value >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo \"ACCEPT $i\" || echo \"reject $i\"; done   # the guarded arm accepts the one it must reject and rejects the one it must accept`

### a-hypothesis-list-is-a-snapshot-of-what-you-knew-that-day
_An open leaf's hypothesis list is dated evidence — when the project later learns a new mechanism, nothing goes back and re-reads it_

- **answers:** I opened a leaf with two hypotheses and the answer turned out to be neither — where did the process fail | we discovered a measurement trap; what else in the backlog is now wrong | how stale is an unworked task leaf | is it worth re-reading a queued leaf before working it | why did a wrong diagnosis survive three sessions in a tracked system | what should happen to open work items when a new trap is documented
- **date:** 2026-08-16 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.19 slice 1, 2026-08-16 session #241. `.19` was opened in session #232 because a re-derived SystemVerilog parser came out 99 747 bytes from the tracked artifact; it named two hypotheses (the flip's diff perturbed codegen / the git-ignored input JSON moved) and priced the measurements that would separate them. Both were wrong. The real mechanism — a generated parser embeds its own `-o` path once per rule-entry site, so 33 249 sites × 3 characters of path difference = 99 747 bytes, exactly — was discovered by the SAME TREE six sessions later, in session #238 (`.20` slice 3), where it inverted that slice's first reading before a normalisation step was added. Nothing connected the two. The leaf sat at the head of the queue for three further sessions carrying hypotheses the project already had the evidence to refute, and the refutation cost 1 m 44 s once it was attempted.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/es19_path_embedding/probe.sh   # exit 0; ARM 2 re-derives the 99 747 and ARM 3 proves the path is the ONLY difference`

### a-keyword-consumed-as-a-keyword-is-not-an-over-acceptance-when-the-standard-gives-it-that-role-outside-its-keyword-list
_A keyword the falsifier proves CONSUMED AS A KEYWORD is still not a dialect over-acceptance when the profile's own standard gives the word that role outside its reserved-word list — IEEE 1364-2005 clause 19.8 spells `timescale's time_unit as s / ms / us / ns / ps / fs and Annex B lists no directive's arguments — and the census earns such a row with a fourth mechanical leg, never with a note_

- **answers:** the verilog_2005 keyword-faithfulness census refuses with fs / ms / ns / ps / us reachable and no witness — are the time units an over-acceptance | is `ns` a reserved word in IEEE 1364-2005 — why does `timescale 1 ns / 1 ps parse if Annex B does not list it | leg 3 says the keyword was consumed as a keyword (the substituted witness rejects) — when is that verdict wrong | what is leg 4 of the keyword-faithfulness census — the identifier witness and the backtick-line rule | what does the fourth column of v2005_keyword_faithfulness/witnesses/MANIFEST.tsv mean | what does verdict directive_argument mean in census.tsv / census.md | how do I prove a keyword is reserved only inside a compiler directive and stays an identifier elsewhere | why are s / ms / us / ns / ps / fs reachable under verilog_2005 only since 1.0.217 | does `wire ns;` parse under verilog_2005 — and should it
- **date:** 2026-09-07 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.39 (release 1.0.217, ledger SV-0090). Typing the compiler directives made time_unit reachable under verilog_2005 through timescale_directive alone (time_literal stays SV-only), and stimuli/sv/v2005_keyword_faithfulness_census.py refused: 5 reachable IEEE-1800-only keyword(s) have no witness: ['fs', 'ms', 'ns', 'ps', 'us'] (rust/target/s339/step_kw_v2005.log). Release probe, verilog_2005: `timescale 1 ns / 1 ps + module m; endmodule ACCEPTS; with ns swapped for zzq_census_ident REJECTS (leg 3: consumed as a keyword); module m; wire ns; wire ps, fs, ms, us; assign ns = ps; endmodule ACCEPTS, and still accepts after the swap (the parser has not reserved the word). IEEE 1364-2005 docs/verilog/2005/md/section-19-compiler-directives.md:557-575 (`timescale time_unit / time_precision; the unit symbols) and Annex B (no directive argument listed). Leg 4 coded in the census (VERDICT_DIRECTIVE_ARGUMENT, the manifest's optional fourth column, refusals for a word used off a backtick-led line, a missing or load-bearing identifier witness); five witness pairs under docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/v2005_keyword_faithfulness/witnesses/; probe.sh section [9] fires each refusal and shows the verdict column MOVING to over_acceptance when the identifier witness rejects.`
- **reverify:** `python3 stimuli/sv/v2005_keyword_faithfulness_census.py | grep -o 'over_acceptances=[0-9]* .*directive_argument=[0-9]*'   # over_acceptances=0 … directive_argument=5; bash docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/v2005_keyword_faithfulness/probe.sh | tail -1   # pass=18 fail=0`

### a-keyword-the-identifier-rule-does-not-refuse-is-an-identifier
_A keyword the identifier rule does not refuse IS an identifier — derive the reserved set from Annex B, and know that no certificate, corpus lane or lint can see a word that rule admits_

- **answers:** PGEN parses `reg global;` / `var final;` / `i.super.i = 1;` — a SystemVerilog keyword is accepted as a variable or hierarchical name | `function new; input x;` parses in a class — the constructor rule is right, so why does the body accept a tf_port_declaration | which IEEE 1800-2017 keywords does the SV grammar reserve — is the list Annex B Table B.1, and how is that checked | how do I regenerate the reserved-word regex from the LRM tables (stimuli/sv/check_sv_reserved_keywords.py --write) | PGEN accepts `automatic int x;` in a package or module — Annex A footnote 10 | PGEN accepts `parameter A;` in a module body — Annex A footnote 18's parameter half | how do I see which production derived a token in a file (parseability_probe --parse-dump-ast-pretty, then walk to the token's name.body) | why did adding a keyword to the reserved list need a twin rule for the randsequence code block | `x < local::x` inside randomize() with { } fails at the x — A.8.4 class_qualifier's local:: had no production | the interpreter (--interpret-parse) rejects `mailbox #(int) m = new(4);` but the generated parser accepts it — is the interpreter faithful for std / provisional class types | a Verilog-2005 test names a variable var / global / local and the sv lane now rejects it — how is the key corrected (edition_keyword_pass)

### a-lexical-adjacency-rule-needs-a-glued-terminal
_A lexical adjacency rule needs a glued terminal — a whitespace-insensitive grammar cannot say "no layout between these two tokens" without the rule-level @glued directive, and the two workarounds each cost something a consumer sees_

- **answers:** why did PGEN reject #1 s = 0 and trans ##1 s before release 1.0.226 — a time unit after white space read as a time literal | is 1 ns with a space a SystemVerilog time literal — IEEE 1800-2017 Annex A footnote 44 | what does the @glued directive do in a PGEN grammar and where is it read | why could the SystemVerilog grammar not spell the time-literal adjacency rule with regexes alone — layout skip, capture groups, lookaround | why does the `timescale directive still accept 1 ns / 1 ps with spaces | can a @glued rule contain a string literal terminal — no, generation refuses
- **date:** 2026-09-08 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.55 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0385, release 1.0.226, ledger SV-0099) and ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.103. On the 1.0.225 probe: `module m; logic s; initial #1 s = 0; endmodule` furthest_position=33; `trans ##1 s;` with `sequence s` furthest_position=133 while `trans ##1 t;`, `trans ##1 (s);`, `trans ##1 s_x;` parse; `trans ##1 ms;` @161, `trans ##1 ps ##1 ns;` @165. Removing the `trivia` prefix from the unit terminals on a candidate copy changed nothing in the interpreter (`#1 s = 0` @33 both sides). A string literal's AST body is `\"\\\"hi\\\"\"` — a regex atom's `$n` is its whole match. Corpus by token: 5 failing lane files carry `<number> <white space> <unit>` after `#` or `##`, 0 accepted; 240 accepted files carry glued time literals.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_delay_then_variable_named_like_a_unit.sv --profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -q 'parse_full passed' && ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_spaced_time_literal_in_timeprecision.sv --profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -q 'furthest_position='`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-lexical-adjacency-rule-needs-a-glued-terminal.md`](docs/knowledge/a-lexical-adjacency-rule-needs-a-glued-terminal.md)

### a-lexical-fact-lives-in-the-terminals-regex
_A lexical fact lives in the terminal's regex — a directive line that ends at the first newline, or a literal that admits only spaces and tabs between its tokens, is a claim about the language's lexis, and clauses 5 and 22 are its source_

- **answers:** why did PGEN reject a multi-line `` `define `` with backslash continuation lines before release 1.0.227 | how does IEEE 1800-2017 22.5.1 continue macro text over lines — the newline preceded by a backslash | may a based literal's size, base and digits be separated by newlines or comments — 5.7.1 and 5.3 | is 5 ' b 01010 legal — no, the apostrophe and the base format character shall not be separated | what does opaque_directive_line match in the SystemVerilog grammar | why did a census of comments inside numbers find English apostrophes — blank the comments first
- **date:** 2026-09-09 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.56 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0386, release 1.0.227, ledger SV-0100). On the 1.0.226 probe: a `` `define `` whose text continues over four backslash-newlines furthest_position=29 (the first continuation line) while the one-line macro parses; `5 'b 01010` parses, `5 <newline> 'b <newline> 01010` furthest_position=40, with block comments 67, with a line comment 60, and `5 ' b 01010` 40 (correctly). Corpus by token: a backslash-continued `` `define `` in 500 failing SV-lane files and 3 accepted; a based literal with a newline or comment between its tokens in 1 failing file and 0 accepted once comments were blanked — the unblanked count was fourteen English apostrophes.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_define_continuation_lines.sv --profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -q 'parse_full passed' && ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_based_literal_space_after_apostrophe.sv --profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -q 'furthest_position='`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-lexical-fact-lives-in-the-terminals-regex.md`](docs/knowledge/a-lexical-fact-lives-in-the-terminals-regex.md)

### a-lexical-terminal-is-edition-specific-too-and-the-regex-crates-dot-stops-at-a-newline
_A lexical terminal is edition-specific too — IEEE 1800 §5.9, 1800-2023 §5.9 and IEEE 1364-2005 §3.6 spell the string literal three ways, the one regex that served all three was wrong for each in a different direction, and the regex crate's `.` stops at a newline so `\\.` is not "backslash plus any character_

- **answers:** why did PGEN reject a SystemVerilog string literal continued with a backslash at the end of the line | is a backslash-newline continuation inside a string literal legal in IEEE 1800-2017 5.9 and in IEEE 1364-2005 3.6 | is a raw newline inside a double-quoted string literal legal SystemVerilog or Verilog | what is a triple-quoted string in IEEE 1800-2023 5.9 and which PGEN profile accepts it | why is verilator t_display_qqq.v must_reject on the sv_2017 lane and must_accept on the sv_2023 lane | why is iverilog ivltests/string12.v must_reject on the verilog_2005 lane | does the Rust regex crate's dot match a newline — what to write for any character in a PGEN terminal | how is a lexical terminal split by profile in the SystemVerilog grammar — the SELECTION-dispatcher pattern for terminals | how does the parse-cost ratchet accept the frame a profile dispatcher adds — the leaf-twin arm of introduced_wrapper_frames | why does the string literal's body keep the backslash and the newline of a continuation | how was the population of string-literal continuations in the corpus censused before the fix
- **date:** 2026-09-08 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.47 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0377, release 1.0.221, ledger SV-0094). Release probe 28948d5cd63c747d… (1.0.220): `$display(\"broken \\` + newline + `line\");` furthest_position=29 on every profile; `$display(\"raw` + newline + `newline\");` parse_full passed on every profile. Interpreter A/B HEAD vs candidate (rust/target/s347/ab_347.tsv): the continuation false -> true on sv_2017 / sv_2023 and unchanged false on verilog_2005, the raw newline true -> false on all three, the triple-quoted forms false -> true on sv_2023 alone, every control ast=SAME. Final bytes: AST-IDENTITY-SWEEP ast_moved=0 on every lane, verdict_moved 5 / 6 / 0 exactly the pre-registered rows; bar 92 -> 86; certificates 1493/10/1468/15 + 1483/0 and 1186/370/802/14. IEEE 1800-2017 §5.9 docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-32-h-12ab-f001.md:101-102; 1800-2023 §5.9 docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-5-lexical-conventions.md:436-464; 1364-2005 §3.6 docs/verilog/2005/md/section-3-lexical-conventions.md:299, A.8.8 docs/verilog/2005/md/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax-definition.md:1218.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_string_line_continuation.sv --profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -q 'parse_full passed' && ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_string_line_continuation_v2005.sv --profile verilog_2005 >/dev/null 2>&1; test $? -ne 0 && ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_string_raw_newline.sv --profile sv_2017 >/dev/null 2>&1; test $? -ne 0 && ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_string_triple_quoted_sv2023.sv --profile sv_2023 2>&1 | grep -q 'parse_full passed'`

### a-line-bound-alternative-must-be-ordered-and-an-empty-matching-regex-is-how-a-grammar-sees-the-newline
_Two engine facts a line-oriented construct rests on — the SystemVerilog grammar's DEFAULT branch policy is a longest-match tournament (a line-bound alternative loses to a run-on one unless the rule is @branch_policy ordered), and a regex terminal that CAN match the empty string is offered only horizontal white space by the layout skip, which is the only way a rule can assert end-of-line_

- **answers:** why did `pragma once followed by foo u1(); parse foo as a pragma keyword — the bare-name alternative was first | what is the SystemVerilog grammar's default branch policy — ordered PEG choice or a tournament | when do I need @branch_policy: ordered on a rule | how can a rule in the SV grammar see a newline when the layout skip eats all white space before every terminal | what does can_match_empty change in consume_layout_for_regex — horizontal skip only | how is `line's 'only white space may appear on the same line, comments are not allowed' enforced | is a newline between compiler-directive arguments legal — `timescale 1ns / newline / 1ps | how do I bound a directive with an optional argument list to its line without a lexer | a regex ending in (?:\\r?\\n|$) — is it can_match_empty, and does the interpreter agree with codegen | a scratch grammar shows the end-of-line regex works but the same rule fails in the SV grammar — what differs | the certificate's probe sample reads `celldefineendmodule or `pragmawj — why does the generator fuse a backtick-led token to the next word | the certificate reports sample_parse_failures on `timescale 100 fs ///x — why is the / separator gone | does a @sample annotation change the generated parser's bytes
- **date:** 2026-09-06 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.39 (release 1.0.217, ledger SV-0090, schema 28 -> 29). (1) pragma_directive := kw_dir_pragma pragma_name pragma_line_end -> {...expressions: []} | kw_dir_pragma pragma_name pragma_expression_list -> {...} on 'module m; `pragma once / foo u1(); endmodule' REJECTED at u1 through the interpreter (accepted=false furthest_position=34, rust/target/s339/micro/g.sv) although alternative 1 matched: the grammar's default policy is longest_match (TOOLBOX 5.1 names it; the annotation vocabulary is @branch_policy: ordered | priority_first | longest_match) and alternative 2 consumed one token more (foo as a pragma_keyword). @branch_policy: ordered -> accepted=true furthest_position=46; the tracked pin control_directive_pragma_line_bound.sv holds it with arm compiler_directive>pragma,module_instantiation. (2) consume_layout_for_regex(can_match_empty, pattern) in the generated parser and the interpreter both skip only HORIZONTAL white space when the anchored regex matches the empty string (codegen regex_pattern_layout_facts, interpreter regex_can_match_empty: the same \\A(?:pattern) probe on ''), so line_end := /[ \\t]*(?:\\r?\\n|$)/ sees the newline every other terminal skips; a three-rule scratch grammar through the interpreter read 'a once\\nb' accepted with e=\"\\n\" and 'a once b' rejected at 6 before the SV rules were trusted. The same pattern spelled non-empty-matching (/[ \\t]*\\r?\\n/) is skipped past its own newline and can never match. (3) Every other directive lets its arguments cross a newline — IEEE 1800-2017 5.3 makes a newline white space and only 22.12 states a line rule — so control_directive_args_across_newline.sv flips fail -> pass on 1.0.217.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline grammars/systemverilog.ebnf --interpret-parse stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_directive_pragma_line_bound.sv --grammar-profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -o 'accepted=[a-z]*'   # true; ./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline grammars/systemverilog.ebnf --interpret-parse stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_directive_line_comment_on_line.sv --grammar-profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -o 'accepted=[a-z]* furthest_position=[0-9]*'   # false@13 — line_end refused the comment; grep -n -B1 '^pragma_directive :=' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf | grep -c 'branch_policy: ordered'   # 1`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-line-bound-alternative-must-be-ordered-and-an-empty-matching-regex-is-how-a-grammar-sees-the-newline.md`](docs/knowledge/a-line-bound-alternative-must-be-ordered-and-an-empty-matching-regex-is-how-a-grammar-sees-the-newline.md)

### a-live-count-in-doctrine-prose-is-derived-state-wearing-a-sentence
_A live count in doctrine prose is derived state wearing a sentence — cite history freely, never a present-tense number the tree can move; and a "cited number must appear in the enforcer" gate is ~95 % false positives, so the rule is R1/R3, not a gate_

- **answers:** how many of the doctrine descriptions disagree with their own enforcer | should the enforcer header be derived from the registry row | a doctrine's description quotes a count — how do I know it is still true | can I gate that every number a doctrine row cites appears in its check script | where may a founding measurement live and where may a live count not | the registry row, the §10 row and the book say the same number — is it current
- **date:** 2026-09-02 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13v / PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0338. `docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/doctrine_prose_census/census.py` over all 34 doctrines: 44 numbers cited in a registry or §10 row that the enforcer's text never contains. Read one by one: 38 founding history, 1 register-read constant, 3 live and true, 2 LIVE AND ROTTED — `LIVE-DOC-CURRENCY` said `CHANGES.md scores 175` (the enforcer's own `20\\d{2}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}` pattern finds 206), `PARSE-COST-RATCHET` said `131 declared LR names, 131 classified` (`--verify-families` reads 41 / 41; `git log -S` dates the 131 to 2026-08-15). Each sat in three reader-facing homes. A presence gate would have fired on 42 of 44 correct numbers.`
- **reverify:** `python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/doctrine_prose_census/census.py 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -1   # DOCTRINE-PROSE-CENSUS: rows=34 … — compare against after_headline.txt beside it; every new lead is READ, not counted`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-live-count-in-doctrine-prose-is-derived-state-wearing-a-sentence.md`](docs/knowledge/a-live-count-in-doctrine-prose-is-derived-state-wearing-a-sentence.md)

### a-lookahead-is-a-child-and-the-template-must-count-it
_A lookahead is a CHILD of the sequence it guards — a positional template must count it, and no gate that compares a release with its predecessor can see a binding that was ALWAYS wrong_

- **answers:** I put a !x guard in front of a rule and now $1 is empty — which slot is the identifier | my list template [$1, $2::2*] returns comma nodes instead of the items after the first | does a negative lookahead occupy a positional slot in a return annotation | how can an AST have been wrong for 150 releases with every gate green | the AST identity sweep read ast_moved=0 — does that prove the tree is right | how do I pin an AST shape so the pin FAILS on the old parser and passes on the new one | why is a typed rule's default type missing from the AST

### a-memo-key-must-name-every-context-the-outcome-depends-on

### a-metrics-root-set-is-part-of-its-meaning
_A reachability metric's ROOT SET is part of its meaning — `unreachable_rules=0` does not mean no rule is unreachable from your entry_

- **answers:** the linter says unreachable_rules=0 but the certificate pass says N rules have no reach path from the entry — which one is wrong | how do I adjudicate the dead-rule candidates --report-certificate-coverage warns about | why does --lint-grammar not flag a rule nothing references | is an unreferenced rule unreachable | which tool finds rules that are reachable only from an orphan root | my grammar lint is green but rules are still UNKNOWN in cert coverage | how do I tell a grammar's dead code from PGEN's own LR-elimination residue | a rule is UNKNOWN and the lint is clean — what do I run next | does a green well-formedness lint mean the grammar has no unreachable rules
- **date:** 2026-08-22 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.16.1 (`PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0164`). `ebnf` / `return_annotation` / `semantic_annotation` each read `--lint-grammar` `unreachable_rules=0, exit 0` while `--report-certificate-coverage` named **31 / 2 / 31** rules with `NO reach path from the entry`. Cause, in the detector's own doc-comment (`rust/src/ast_pipeline/grammar_wellformedness.rs:386`): roots = the canonical entry PLUS every rule NOTHING references. Both readings are correct; they quantify over different root sets. The 64 split further into **9 LR-elimination residue + 55 source orphans** once the PRE-elimination raw AST is compared against the POST-elimination gen-AST.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline grammars/ebnf.ebnf --lint-grammar | grep -o 'unreachable_rules=[0-9]*'   # 0 — then: python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/grammar_wellformed/residual_island_census/probe.py --grammar ebnf --entry grammar_file   # post_outside=31 lr_residue=4 source_orphans=27 islands=14`

### a-minimal-core-is-a-witness-only-for-the-vintage-it-was-shrunk-under
_A minimal reproducer is minimised AGAINST ONE ARTIFACT — carried to another vintage it can flip while the row it came from does not, so a core is a witness for the vintage it was shrunk under and for no other_

- **answers:** my minimal repro behaves differently on an older commit than the full input does | can I use a shrunk test case to bisect across versions | the reduced case says the fix regressed but the original input says it did not | is a delta-debugged core a faithful stand-in for its input | how do I attribute a rejected row to a specific change | why does my minimised case disagree with the ledger | should I re-shrink a reproducer when I change the artifact under test

### a-missing-alternative-is-invisible-to-every-instrument-that-reads-only-what-exists
_A dropped member of a keyword enumeration is invisible to every instrument that reads only what the grammar DECLARES — the lint resolves every name, the certificate witnesses every rule that exists, the corpus sees it only where a file spells the word; only a census against the standard's own enumeration can see it_

- **answers:** lint, certificates and the corpus are all green, so can a keyword alternation still be missing a member | why did nothing catch net_type shipping ten of the LRM's twelve alternatives | how do I check every LRM keyword enumeration against the shipped grammar at once | what does LRM-KEYWORD-ENUMERATION measure and what does it deliberately not score | is a trailing digit on an LRM production name a footnote marker or part of the name | why does the LRM extractor merge strength0 and strength1 into one rule | an instrument reports a shipped rule reaches keywords the LRM enumeration lacks, is that an over-acceptance | a keyword is reserved by the standard and the profile accepts it, so why is it still an over-acceptance | the keyword-admission census is green, can a profile still accept a keyword in a position its standard never allows | which census catches a legal keyword in an illegal position | the LRM extractor merged two productions into one rule, what does the grammar now accept that it should not
- **date:** 2026-09-01 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `LRM-GRAMMAR-FIDELITY.1e (PGEN-LRM-GRAMMAR-FIDELITY-0001), discharging SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13n(e). net_type shipped 10 of the LRM's 12 alternatives for the whole life of the flattened grammar (ledger SV-0075) with --lint-grammar green, the certificate pass green and 9 corpus rows failing that no guard attributed. The census stimuli/sv/lrm_keyword_enumeration_census.py joins the vendored Annex A markdown (read with the extractor's own scraping primitives, pinned equal to extract_rules on 734/747/381 rules) to the shipped grammar's raw_ast envelope under each edition's profile: 109 enumerations, 97 name-matched, 289 keyword members, 0 MISSING at HEAD; a RED control that removes the two net_type branches from a copy of the shipped grammar reads MISSING 6 of 6 with exactly six rows moving. Reusing the extractor's canonicalize_rule_name reported strength0 missing strong and weak, members the LRM never wrote: that canonicaliser strips trailing digits unconditionally and merges strength0/strength1 and delay2/delay3 in all three editions (grammars/systemverilog_lrm_profiled_generated.ebnf:1860 carries strength := kw_supply | kw_strong | kw_pull | kw_weak). The extra column's first customer was edge in 1364-2005 edge_identifier ::= posedge | negedge, confirmed a verilog_2005 over-acceptance by three probe legs (SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13o).`
- **reverify:** `python3 stimuli/sv/lrm_keyword_enumeration_census.py --grammar grammars/systemverilog.ebnf | head -1`
