### a-non-zero-value-hides-a-missing-addend
_A non-zero value hides a missing addend — the row where the count goes to ZERO is the only one where an incomplete sum becomes a visible contradiction_

- **answers:** my counter looks plausible everywhere; how would I know a term is missing | two of my instruments disagree on one row and agree everywhere else — what does that mean | where should I look first when auditing a published count | I added a new code path; what else needs changing | how did an under-reported number survive across many releases | is a matching total good corroboration
- **date:** 2026-08-16 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.27, 2026-08-16 session #241. A grammar linter published `left_recursion_eliminated=N`, taken from the elimination pass's own outcome. A second pass (indirect elimination) had been added earlier along with its own outcome fields, and the lint's call site was never extended to read them - so the headline counted only the direct pass. Across eleven grammars the omission was invisible on ten of them - SystemVerilog published 2 where the true figure is 5, and "the pass did something" reads as correct. On the eleventh, `ebnf`, the direct count was ZERO while the generated parser demonstrably carried six `_lr_*` rule names emitted by the eliminator, so the published value read as "nothing was eliminated" and two instruments openly contradicted each other. That contradiction is what opened the investigation. The names the count had been hiding were `casting_type` and `property_expr` - the two rules the entire surrounding campaign was about.`
- **reverify:** `ast_pipeline grammars/ebnf.ebnf --lint-grammar | head -1   # left_recursion_eliminated=1 (info — 0 direct + 1 indirect); before the fix this read 0 while generated/ebnf.rs declared 6 _lr_* names`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-non-zero-value-hides-a-missing-addend.md`](docs/knowledge/a-non-zero-value-hides-a-missing-addend.md)

### a-number-read-out-of-context-carries-a-frame-you-did-not-measure
_A value lifted out of a grid, a log line or a process listing arrives with a FRAME attached — the boundary, the file, the root — and the frame is the part you did not measure_

- **answers:** I sampled a grid and the first failure was at point N — can I publish N as the boundary | I read a line number out of a compiler warning — is that the file's length | ps shows a process writing a file I care about — is it writing MY copy of that file | how do I tell a measured quantity from a quantity plus an assumed context | my evidence is real and my conclusion is still wrong — where did it go | I printed a count that refutes my claim and explained it away — what should I have done | what does a zero in my own diagnostic output actually license me to conclude | a relative path appeared in my evidence — what do I owe before acting on it | why do three unrelated mistakes in one session feel like the same mistake | is a single sample enough to publish a per-unit cost
- **date:** 2026-08-31 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.87(d) / PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0160. THREE published claims in one session, all withdrawn under director challenge, all the same shape. (1) A 12-point spawn-size grid returned OK at 64 TiB and FAILED at 128 TiB; published as 'the first refusal is at 128 TiB, the reservation an 8 PiB host would derive'. Bisected: the boundary is 2^46 = 64.000 TiB exactly, so the smallest host that could derive a refused reservation is 4 PiB, not 8. A grid cannot locate a boundary. (2) A clippy warning cited generated/systemverilog_parser.rs:1582679; published as a '1.58 M-line generated SV parser'. wc -l says 1 709 231 — a line NUMBER is not a file LENGTH. (3) ps showed a live second `claude` session running `python3` with `p='DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md'`; published as 'a second Claude Code session is live in THIS repository and is writing a tracked live doc', with a commit-safety mitigation attached. The path was RELATIVE and was resolved against the wrong root: `lsof -a -p <pid> -d cwd` says /Volumes/SSD/Documents/github/anvil, and CLAIM-SHAPE-SHADOW-RUN is an anvil task tree that git grep finds nowhere in pgen. PGEN's DEVELOPMENT_NOTES.md was untouched throughout. The refuting evidence had ALREADY been printed in the same message — `lsof -p 62750 | grep -c pgen` returned 0 — and was explained away as 'the write has not landed yet'.`
- **reverify:** `lsof -a -p $(pgrep -n claude) -d cwd    # a process's cwd is what a RELATIVE path in its argv hangs from; ps alone never tells you the root. Then the general form on any grid-derived boundary: re-run the probe as a BISECTION between the last OK and the first FAIL and compare the two answers.`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-number-read-out-of-context-carries-a-frame-you-did-not-measure.md`](docs/knowledge/a-number-read-out-of-context-carries-a-frame-you-did-not-measure.md)

### a-package-name-lives-in-its-own-name-space
_A package name lives in its own name space — a scope gate that consults the type name space to refuse a package name refuses legal text; gate the scope on the fact of the thing it names, and keep the exclusion for when that fact is absent_

- **answers:** why did PGEN reject T::VALUE when a typedef named T was visible beside package T before release 1.0.225 | can a package and a typedef share a name in SystemVerilog — IEEE 1800-2017 3.13 name spaces | does import p::* make a typedef T shadow package T — 26.3 potentially locally visible | what does non_typedef_package_scope gate in the SystemVerilog grammar and why is it an ordered choice | how was the package-scope fix kept free on the parse-cost sample — branch-local predicates instead of a dispatcher | is std::randomize(obj.x) legal — 18.12 Syntax 18-11 variable_identifier_list | is extern function f(in); legal without a return type — A.2.6 function_prototype | is a virtual function prototype without a body legal in a class — A.1.9 class_method pure virtual or extern | is a trailing comma legal in a port connection list — A.4.1.1 list_of_port_connections

- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.54 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0384, release 1.0.225, ledger SV-0098). On the 1.0.224 probe: `package T; parameter int VALUE = 23; endpackage module test; initial if (T::VALUE !== 23) $stop; endmodule` parse_full passed; the same after `package p; typedef int T; endpackage import p::*;` furthest_position=132 (the VALUE after T::); after a unit-level `typedef int T;` furthest_position=95; `typedef int T;` with no package furthest_position=45 (correct). Predicate trace (--trace-rules ps_parameter_identifier,scoped_package_parameter_identifier,non_typedef_package_scope,class_scope): non_typedef_package_scope rejected by post predicate lacks_fact_attribute_equals [type_name, T, declaration_family, typedef], then every class-scope arm refused. Corpus census by token: 1 failing SV-lane file with a package and a typedef of one name (iverilog sv_type_identifier_package_name.v), 0 accepted files; 15 accepted files use a typedef name as a X:: prefix.`

### a-parenthesised-operator-assignment-is-an-expression-and-so-an-operand
_A parenthesised operator assignment is an expression and so an operand — a grammar that flattens the binary chain into operand-step must admit every A.8.3 expression form as an operand, and the form is IEEE 1800's, not 1364's_

- **answers:** why did PGEN reject j = i++ + (i = i - 1) — IEEE 1800-2017 11.4.2's own example — before release 1.0.224 | is a parenthesised assignment legal as an operand of a binary operator in SystemVerilog — A.8.3 ( operator_assignment ) | is j = (i = i - 1) legal Verilog-2005 — IEEE 1364-2005 A.8.3 expression has no assignment inside an expression | what is paren_operator_assignment_operand / expression_chain_operand in the SystemVerilog grammar | why is expression_chain_operand an ordered choice and why does that change no verdict | how did the top-level parenthesised assignment keep a byte-identical AST when the operand form was added — expression_chain_step+ as the chain head | does a constant expression admit ( P = 3 ) — no, A.8.3 constant_expression has no assignment
- **date:** 2026-09-08 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.53 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0383, release 1.0.224, ledger SV-0097). On the 1.0.223 probe: j = (i = i - 1); parse_full passed, j = 1 + (i = i - 1); furthest_position=38, (i = i - 1) + 1 @43; ispras 11.04.02_01.sv @230, sv-tests 11.3.6--two_assign_in_expr.sv @476 and -sim @530; integer i, j; initial j = (i = i - 1); parse_full passed under verilog_2005. Interpreter A/B HEAD vs candidate, 17 files × 3 profiles: the three corpus rows and the operand control false → true on the SV profiles, the v2005 form true → false under verilog_2005 alone, every other arm ast=SAME. Census by token: 5 operand-form files and 13 top-level-form files on the SV lanes, 0 and 0 on the verilog_2005 lane.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_paren_operator_assignment_operand.sv --profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -q 'parse_full passed' && ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_paren_operator_assignment_top_level.sv --profile sv_2017 2>&1 | grep -q 'parse_full passed' && ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_paren_operator_assignment_v2005.sv --profile verilog_2005 2>&1 | grep -q 'furthest_position=' && grep -q '^paren_operator_assignment_operand :=' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf && echo OK`

### a-per-branch-fact-joined-against-a-rule-level-profile-set-over-reports
_`@profiles` is RULE-level, so joining a per-BRANCH fact against `satisfiable_under` over-reports by construction — on SystemVerilog every single row that join produced was a false positive_

- **answers:** my @sample does not parse under a profile — is that a defect | how do I tell a dead alternative from a wrong annotation | why does my profile census report defects that are all correct | how do I get per-alternative profile satisfiability out of PGEN | can a rule be live under a profile while some of its alternatives are dead | how do I join branch_semantic_annotations against profile data | why did gating a terminal make an unrelated rule go UNKNOWN
- **date:** 2026-08-26 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.11(a), PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0307. `@profiles` is a rule-level annotation, but 43 of SystemVerilog's 52 `@sample` annotations are branch-level. Measured over the whole grammar with docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/sample_profile_parity/sample_profile_parity.py: the RULE-level join (`satisfiable_under`) reports 8 defects over 115 checks and ALL EIGHT ARE FALSE POSITIVES; the BRANCH-level join (`branch_satisfiable_under`, added by this leaf) reports 0 over 101. The 8 are exactly the 7 SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.9 had adjudicated BY HAND as 'branch DEAD under v2005 — sample honest' (block_data_type 3/4, data_type 3/4, case_statement 1, module_declaration_sv_2017 3/4) plus the 1 that PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0305 created (module_declaration_sv_2017 branch 2, whose mandatory dot_star was gated out of verilog_2005) — a derived predicate agreeing with an independent hand adjudication on 7 of 7 and supplying the 8th. `-0305` had mis-filed that 8th as a DEFECT precisely by joining on the owning RULE, and published the wrong attribution to a task leaf AND to the tracked contract rust/test_data/grammar_quality/verilog_2005_conformance_contract_v0.json, both corrected here. derive_branch_profiles (rust/src/ast_pipeline/grammar_wellformedness.rs) reuses compute_sat_by_profile/node_satisfiable — the profile-orphan lint's own fixpoint — so there is no second model of the grammar; the union of a rule's per-branch sets equals its satisfiable_under on 1537 of 1537 SV rules.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline grammars/systemverilog.ebnf --dump-rule-profiles rp.json >/dev/null && python3 -c \"import json;d=json.load(open('rp.json'))['rules']['module_declaration_sv_2017'];print('rule:',d['satisfiable_under']);print('branches:',d['branch_satisfiable_under'])\"   # the rule reads [sv_2017, verilog_2005]; branches 2/3/4 read [sv_2017] alone. Then: python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/sample_profile_parity/sample_profile_parity.py --grammar grammars/systemverilog.ebnf   (0 defects / 101 checks) versus --join rule   (8 defects / 115 checks, all false).`

### a-poller-that-matches-its-own-command-line-never-terminates
_A wait-loop built on `pgrep -f "<pattern>"` matches its OWN command line, so the condition can never go false — the job finishes and the watcher reports it running forever_

- **answers:** my until-pgrep wait loop never exits even though the job finished | how do I wait for a background build to finish from a shell | why does pgrep -f find my job when the job is not running | how do I poll for a long build without leaving zombie shells behind | my background job status says running but there is no cargo or rustc process | how should I verify that nothing is in flight before declaring a workspace clean
- **date:** 2026-08-19 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `PGEN session 2026-08-19. Six `until ! pgrep -f "cargo build --release --features generated_parsers"; do sleep 30; done` waiters were spawned to block on ~20-minute release builds. Every one embeds the pattern in its own `bash -c` argv, so `pgrep -f` matched the waiters themselves — measured, `pgrep -f "cargo build --release --features generated_parsers"` returned SEVEN bash pids and ZERO cargo processes, with `pgrep -x cargo` and `pgrep -x rustc` both empty. The builds had all completed normally; the watchers ran for roughly two hours after the last one, at `Ss` with ~2 s of CPU each, and would have run until the session ended.`
- **reverify:** `pgrep -f 'until ! pgrep -f' | wc -l   # 0 = no self-matching waiters are alive; and cross-check the WORK with `pgrep -x cargo` / `pgrep -x rustc`, which cannot self-match because -x matches the executable name, not argv`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-poller-that-matches-its-own-command-line-never-terminates.md`](docs/knowledge/a-poller-that-matches-its-own-command-line-never-terminates.md)

### a-precedent-tells-you-what-to-try-not-that-it-works
_A sibling grammar shipping the exact shape is a LEAD, not a verdict — close the facet matrix before adopting it_

- **answers:** another grammar solved this with one directive — can I just copy it | how do I decide whether @whitespace_sensitive is the right fix for my grammar | what do the terminals / regex_tokens / trailing facets actually change | my whitespace rule is never witnessed even though it is referenced from the entry | why is my comment rule witnessed but my whitespace rule is not | how do I test a grammar-level directive without regenerating the parser | is a rule that the layout skipper consumes a dead rule or a reach gap | when should I proof-promote a rule that can never be witnessed
- **date:** 2026-08-22 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.16.4 (`PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0167`). `ebnf.ebnf`'s `whitespace := /(\s+)/` sits in `grammar_file`'s alternation beside `comment` and can never be witnessed — the emitted `consume_layout_for_regex` gates every comment arm on `regex_token_matches_at_cursor(pattern)` but runs `consume_optional_whitespace()` unconditionally. `systemverilog_preprocessor.ebnf:23` fixes the same shape with `@whitespace_sensitive: { regex_tokens: true }`; on `ebnf.ebnf` all four settings of the three-facet directive break reading `grammars/json.ebnf`, and only two even witness the rule.`
- **reverify:** `printf '    ' > /tmp/ws.txt && ./rust/target/debug/ast_pipeline grammars/ebnf.ebnf --interpret-parse /tmp/ws.txt --interpret-parse-ast-json /tmp/ws.json && python3 -c \"import json;print(json.load(open('/tmp/ws.json'))['content'])\"   # elements: [] , span 0..0 — the * ran ZERO iterations`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-precedent-tells-you-what-to-try-not-that-it-works.md`](docs/knowledge/a-precedent-tells-you-what-to-try-not-that-it-works.md)

### a-profile-gate-inverts-every-negative-lookahead-on-the-gated-rule
_A dialect gate silently inverts every negative lookahead on the gated rule — the strict profile gets MORE permissive_

- **answers:** I am about to @profiles-gate a rule — what breaks that no lint will tell me | why did my strict profile start accepting something the permissive one rejects | does a `!X` lookahead still refuse when X is gated out of the active profile | how do I gate a terminal out of a dialect without widening the language | my probe printed verdicts under two profiles and they were identical — is that a result | how do I tell a vacuous lookahead from a refusing one | is a rule named _sv_only actually gated
- **date:** 2026-08-25 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0303, sizing SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.10(c4). Measured on a 5-rule synthetic driven with ast_pipeline --interpret-parse --grammar-profile, with a proven-active control: a REQUIRED gated rule accepts under `loose` and REJECTS under `strict` (so the gate is on), while `!X` with a catch-all able to consume the guarded token REJECTS under `loose` and ACCEPTS under `strict`. --lint-grammar is completely clean on this: no profile_orphans, no unreachable_rules, no warning. Live population in PGEN's SystemVerilog grammar: 3 sites, all !scope_resolution, with scope_resolution gated to [sv_2017, sv_2023]; none produces an over-acceptance today because nothing else under verilog_2005 can consume `::`, so the parse fails on the unconsumable token regardless — the hazard bites only when some other alternative CAN consume what the lookahead guarded against. TWO EARLIER ATTEMPTS TO MEASURE THIS PRODUCED CONFIDENT NON-RESULTS: (1) @profiles written INLINE after := is a BRANCH-level gate and never gated the rule, revealed only by the control arm; (2) the corrected probe could not discriminate, because with nothing able to consume the token a vacuous lookahead and a refusing one both end in a reject.`
- **reverify:** `⛔ MEASURED ON THE INTERPRETER ONLY — the probe makes 0 generated-parser invocations, and TOOLBOX 1.5b marks the interpreter authoritative BY VERIFICATION, not by construction. Reproducing on the shipped engine (scratch slot 1.3 / compile_and_parse 1.4) is step (a) of ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.46 and is OWED. bash docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/profile_gate_sizing/probe.sh   # 6/6, ~1s. Arm [1] is the control that proves the gate is active; arm [2] is the finding: !X rejects under loose and ACCEPTS under strict.`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-profile-gate-inverts-every-negative-lookahead-on-the-gated-rule.md`](docs/knowledge/a-profile-gate-inverts-every-negative-lookahead-on-the-gated-rule.md)

### a-provenance-block-must-say-whether-the-numbers-were-ever-right
_Which tree was this derived from?" and "were the numbers ever right about that tree?" are two questions — a provenance block that answers only the first turns a vague RED into a confident wrong answer_

- **answers:** what fields does an identity or provenance block actually need | can I stamp a freshness block on a baseline that is currently failing | my gate says provenance fresh and then reports a drift nobody can explain | is recording input hashes enough to make a stale baseline diagnosable | how do I adopt provenance on an artifact I cannot re-derive yet | should a provenance state have a default value | why did adding provenance make my gate worse
- **date:** 2026-08-20 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2x.2. Slice 1 (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0248`) stamped `systemverilog_recognized_cert_union_contract.json` with `verified_at_commit` + input digests taken at HEAD — while `.13c.2x` had already MEASURED those expectations wrong at HEAD by 71 rules and 53 UNKNOWNs. The block therefore asserted a derivation that never happened, and the consuming gate printed `identity fresh` and proceeded to a drift report nobody could attribute. Retracted the same day by `-0249`, which added a REQUIRED `expectations: confirmed|unconfirmed` field with no default; the contract is now `unconfirmed` and the gate refuses in under a second, naming the reason and the owning leaf.`
- **reverify:** `bash scripts/check_baseline_identity.sh --verify rust/test_data/grammar_quality/systemverilog_recognized_cert_union_contract.json   # rc=1, ARE UNCONFIRMED, names SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2x`

### a-published-block-derived-from-untracked-state-fails-on-a-clean-clone
_A co-publication gate holds a document equal to a DERIVATION, so the derivation must read only TRACKED inputs — mix in build-output state and the gate fails on a fresh clone while passing on the machine that ran the build_

- **answers:** my derive-and-diff currency gate passes locally and fails in CI — what differs | should a published status block include what the gate artifacts in my tree say | how do I keep a --check style documentation gate portable across clones | why does a status page disagree between two checkouts of the same commit | can I publish a number that comes from something under target/ | how do I report machine-local state without making it a gate-held claim
- **date:** 2026-08-30 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `DONE-BAR-VISIBILITY.1 (PGEN-DONE-BAR-VISIBILITY-0003). scripts/audit_done_bar.sh derives Done-bar leg 1 and the green-NOW half of leg 2 from `*_parser_family_status_gate/summary.txt` artifacts under rust/target/, which .gitignore excludes. On the machine that had run the gate the audit reported leg 1 UNPROVEN with reason `artifact … STALE — older than its own inputs`; driven through its own PGEN_DONE_BAR_TARGET_DIR seam at an empty directory — the state of any fresh clone — the same commit reported `has produced no non-empty summary.txt on this machine`. Same verdict, different sentence: a block publishing either one would fail --check for the other reader. Measured on the same run: with the seam applied the audit's whole report carries no mtimes and no build-output paths, so the tracked-only derivation is byte-stable across clones, and all 13 of the audit's ground-truth controls still reproduce.`
- **reverify:** `mkdir -p rust/target/empty && PGEN_DONE_BAR_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/rust/target/empty bash scripts/audit_done_bar.sh | grep -A2 'leg 1' | head -4   # then diff against `bash scripts/audit_done_bar.sh` — the verdicts agree, the REASONS do not`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-published-block-derived-from-untracked-state-fails-on-a-clean-clone.md`](docs/knowledge/a-published-block-derived-from-untracked-state-fails-on-a-clean-clone.md)

### a-ranking-is-robust-to-an-undercount-that-a-share-is-not
_A classifier wrong about 75.1 % of a rule family moved the SHARE it published by 4x, moved 12.5 % of the sample rows it ranked, and moved the quantity that sample exists to cover by 0.45 % — three different blast radii from one defect_

- **answers:** my classifier was wrong — which of the things built on it actually have to be redone | do I have to re-derive my sampled benchmark after fixing the metric that selected it | how do I decide whether to re-pin a benchmark sample or keep the old one | is it worth resetting a performance baseline to adopt a corrected selection | a measurement bug affected two published numbers — are both equally wrong | how do I price a correction instead of assuming it must propagate everywhere
- **date:** 2026-08-16 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.21 acceptance (b), 2026-08-16. One regex classified PGEN's left-recursion-elimination rule family. It matched 97 of the parser's 127 LR rule names and missed **75.1 %** of the family's corpus rule entries (18 518 719 of 24 644 435). Two things were built on it. (1) A published SHARE, `0.681 %` of all corpus entries — wrong by **4x**; the true figure is 2.741 %, and every surface quoting it was stale. (2) A pinned 192-file benchmark sample whose `lr` tier is *"the 40 heaviest by guarded-admission entries"* — re-derived under the corrected classifier over a reproducible full-corpus census (two censuses, RAW BYTE-IDENTICAL, 16 336 rows each), it moves `hot` **0/40**, `lr` **5/40**, `breadth` **19/112** — **24 of 192 slots, 12.5 % of the sample** — while the LR-family entries that sample COVERS change by only **+0.45 %** (12 440 690 -> 12 496 291). ⛔ Both numbers, always: a first draft of this card published only the 0.45 %, which makes the decision to decline look easier than it is. The correction was necessary and the selection barely noticed it.`
- **reverify:** `python3 stimuli/sv/corpus_parse_cost.py --census --outdir <a> && python3 stimuli/sv/corpus_parse_cost.py --census --outdir <b> && python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/sample_rederivation/compare_sample.py --census-a <a>/census.tsv --census-b <b>/census.tsv   # 4 legs, exit 0; leg 4 is an external oracle — the fresh census must reproduce the tracked entries.tsv totals 416 841 264 / 12 440 690 exactly`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-ranking-is-robust-to-an-undercount-that-a-share-is-not.md`](docs/knowledge/a-ranking-is-robust-to-an-undercount-that-a-share-is-not.md)

### a-reconstruction-of-why-someone-got-a-number-is-a-provenance-claim

- **answers:** an earlier commit published a count I cannot reproduce — how do I explain the difference | my number disagrees with a published one, should I say their method was different | is it safe to assume a previous author used the narrower method | how do I check a claim about WHY someone got a result rather than about the result | I found a charitable explanation for an old discrepancy — what do I have to verify | should I call an old number wrong or method-dependent | how do I audit a reconstruction of someone else's reasoning | my own table contradicts my explanation and I did not notice — how does that happen

Three re-derivations gave 4 (a strict size-class method, a lower bound by construction), 5 (the subset-sum attribution) and 5 (a lifetime tape). -0131 published the charitable reconstruction: the 4 `is what the strict method answers`, so the count was METHOD-DEPENDENT rather than wrong. -0128's own sentence refutes it — it cites `t_math_synmul_mul.v` as its worked example of an input holding two tables, and the strict method sees only ONE there because the second table shares a size class. ### a-refutation-names-what-is-not-the-cause
_Refuting a failure's label from the input's own bytes narrows the cause — it never names it, and it refutes only the labels whose claim those bytes actually bear on_

- **answers:** this corpus row is deferred as needing the preprocessor — can I disprove that from the file itself | the file contains no directive at all and the parse still fails — is the deferral label wrong | my falsification test flagged N rows across several buckets — can I publish that as N misclassifications | how do I tell a multi-file TEXT dependency from a multi-file FACT dependency | why does the parse fail on a type name that is declared in a different file | does a zero-directive file mean the same thing in every deferral class | how do I decide whether expansion or unit-level fact continuity unblocks a deferred corpus row
- **date:** 2026-08-11 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md leaf .13a (the 530-row census, the 3-row probe, the 8 rows read before publishing); docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/verdict_coverage/{coverage.md,strata.tsv}; stimuli/sv/corpus_verdict_coverage.py (TICK_MEANING + the import-time refusal); stimuli/sv/subs/opentitan/hw/dv/sv/csrng_agent/csrng_if.sv (the canonical row — 0 backticks, dies on a sibling file's type name)`

- **answers:** which gates must a SystemVerilog grammar release run on its final bytes (the release ceremony) | sv_syntax_closure_gate is RED with an unreachable rule SET that differs from allowed_unreachable_rules — suppress, list, or delete | BASELINE-IDENTITY says a contract has been STALE across more commits than its budget — what do I do | why did the store-gate memo not re-measure after the instrument changed (memo key = file sha + binary sha only) | a probe bank went RED for several commits and nobody noticed — who runs it now (SV-STORE-GATE-BANK) | check_doctrines.sh passed in CI but the release probe is not built there — which doctrines evaluated nothing | what does PGEN_RELEASE_PROBE do

### a-rule-is-typed-when-every-alternative-carries-a-template-census-the-alternatives-not-the-rule

### a-rule-missing-from-the-active-tree-has-two-causes-and-only-one-is-a-profile-fact
_A rule absent from the active `grammar_tree` is EITHER profile-removed OR never defined, the generator cannot tell which, and treating both as dead broke a passing test_

- **answers:** can I treat a missing rule reference as gated-out by the profile | why did my profile-aware pruning break a grammar with no profiles | how do I tell a profile-filtered rule from an undefined one in the generator | does apply_grammar_profile_filter leave the removed rules in rule_order | how should a reach or reachability pass handle an include() external reference | my analysis pass over-pruned and I cannot tell why
- **date:** 2026-08-26 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.51 slice 1, PGEN-ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES-0089. The reach BFS was taught to skip a hop site whose enclosing alternative the profile filter had killed, keyed on `!grammar_tree.contains_key(name)`. That predicate is TRUE for two unrelated situations: a rule the profile filter removed, and a rule never defined in this grammar at all (PGEN's include(...) system; `node_satisfiable` in grammar_wellformedness.rs deliberately treats the latter as TOP with the comment 'no false positives'). There is no residue to discriminate on: `apply_grammar_profile_filter` (rust/src/main.rs:2657) builds a `retained_rule_order`, so the filter prunes `rule_order` as well as `grammar_tree`, and `StimuliGenerator` holds no profile field at all. Measured consequence: the first cut took the pre-existing test `spurious_store_entry_block_keeps_its_own_rule_witness` RED, because its fixture reaches `soft_target` through an UNDEFINED `epsilon` -- so the whole alternative was pruned and `set_reach_plan_for_rule` would not install. Attribution measured, not assumed: `git checkout HEAD -- stimuli_generator.rs` -> test passes; re-apply -> test fails. Fix: `reach_hops_pass` PREFERS the pruned walk and FALLS BACK to the unpruned one, so pruning can only ever improve a route and never deletes the last one; pinned by `an_undefined_reference_must_not_prune_a_route_the_way_a_profile_gate_does`. Final: 224/224 in the module, verilog_2005 cert UNKNOWN 18 -> 14 with the fallback in place (identical to without it).`
- **reverify:** `cd rust && cargo test --lib stimuli_generator::tests::an_undefined_reference_must_not_prune_a_route_the_way_a_profile_gate_does && cargo test --lib stimuli_generator::tests::spurious_store_entry_block_keeps_its_own_rule_witness`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-rule-missing-from-the-active-tree-has-two-causes-and-only-one-is-a-profile-fact.md`](docs/knowledge/a-rule-missing-from-the-active-tree-has-two-causes-and-only-one-is-a-profile-fact.md)

### a-rule-named-sv-only-is-not-thereby-gated
_A rule named for a dialect is not thereby gated to it — the name and the @profiles annotation are independent, and only one of them is enforced_

- **answers:** a rule is named _sv_2017 / _sv_only — is it actually restricted to that dialect | why does an SV-only construct still parse under my strict dialect profile | how do I audit which dialect-named rules are actually gated | I fixed one rule whose name promised a gate it did not have — is the class closed | what should a naming convention be allowed to carry
- **date:** 2026-08-25 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `Measured in PGEN's SystemVerilog grammar. SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.7 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0290..0293) found `data_declaration_sv_2017` — named for IEEE 1800 — carrying @profiles that ADMIT verilog_2005, and it was the door for 9 measured over-acceptances; the repair was 13 named _sv_only gates over 19 SITES INSIDE it, NOT removing the admission. SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.10(c4) sizing (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0303) then found `.*` reaching verilog_2005 through three more dialect-named-but-admitted hosts (module_declaration_sv_2017, named_port_connection_sv_2017, udp_declaration_sv_2017), while the other four dot_star hosts are correctly [\"sv_2017\"] only. THE CLASS CENSUS, run in that leaf: 27 rules whose name carries a dialect suffix are @profiles-admitted to verilog_2005. ⛔ THAT COUNT IS NOT A DEFECT COUNT AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS ONE — admission usually means the rule genuinely SERVES both profiles despite its name (module_declaration and specify-path descriptions exist in IEEE 1364-2005 too). What the mismatch marks is a SITE WHERE AN SV-ONLY ELEMENT CAN LEAK, which is exactly what .13e.7 and .13e.10 each found. 2 of the 27 have been audited; 25 have not.`
- **reverify:** `python3 - <<'PY'\nimport re,pathlib\nlines=pathlib.Path('grammars/systemverilog.ebnf').read_text().splitlines()\nfor i,l in enumerate(lines):\n    m=re.match(r'^([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(?:_sv_2017|_sv_2023|_sv_only))\\s*:=',l)\n    if not m: continue\n    j,prof=i-1,None\n    while j>=0 and (not lines[j].strip() or lines[j].lstrip().startswith(('#','@'))):\n        p=re.match(r'^@profiles:\\s*(\\[.*\\])',lines[j].strip())\n        if p: prof=p.group(1); break\n        j-=1\n    if prof and 'verilog_2005' in prof: print(f'MISMATCH L{i+1} {m.group(1)} -> {prof}')\nPY`

### a-rules-memo-hit-rate-is-a-property-of-its-call-graph-not-of-the-rule
_A rule's memo-hit rate is a property of how many places call it, not of the rule — so pricing a fix from that rate prices a graph the fix itself moves_

- **answers:** why did my packrat rule report zero memo hits when it is called millions of times | where should I spell a guard — in the shared rule or at its call sites | my cost model used measured memo-hit rates and still came out backwards — why | does adding call sites to a rule make a parser slower | what does a generated parser's inlining do to per-rule counters | how do I compare two spellings of the same grammar fix
- **date:** 2026-08-19 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2k (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0236/-0237, corrected under director challenge in -0238). FOUR parser arms of ONE correctness fix, measured over a pinned 192-file sample, all verdict-identical on every one of the 192 files. The generator's own census gives the decision: a rule is INLINED (and takes no memo lookup at all) while refs x body_nodes stays under a named duplication budget. Baseline: `identifier` refs=47 over-budget/memoized, wrapper refs=7 INLINED. Moving 45 references flips both - `identifier` to refs=1 INLINED, wrapper to refs=52 over-budget/memo-served at 94.5 % hits. designB (guard inside `identifier`, wrapper a bare alias) changed NEITHER decision and cost +1.78 % on entries purely through redirected speculation - refused. designA (wrapper delegates) -0.89 % entries but +0.72 % committed - refused on the other counter. designC (wrapper matches the token) -1.07 % entries, -5.11 % committed, -2.41 % memo hits - shipped. The difference, read out of the generated parser rather than inferred: the wrapper rule `non_keyword_identifier` is reached through 341 generated `inlined_frame_call` sites in designB, which bypass its own memoization (14,320,942 entries / 0 memo hits); giving it 45 more grammar references makes it memo-served (18,758,343 entries / 17,724,671 hits = 94.5 %) and the inner rule then runs 1,516,324 bodies instead of 19,353,115 entries.`
- **reverify:** `python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/strictness_cost_arms/inline_decision.py   # prints the GENERATOR's own inline verdict (class, refs, body_nodes, INLINED|over-budget) for each arm of the fix, beside the duplication budget it is judged against. Do NOT substitute counts of `inlined_frame_call` in the generated parser: those are emitted sites after transitive expansion, and reading them as the decision is the error this card was corrected for`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-rules-memo-hit-rate-is-a-property-of-its-call-graph-not-of-the-rule.md`](docs/knowledge/a-rules-memo-hit-rate-is-a-property-of-its-call-graph-not-of-the-rule.md)

### a-scope-hides-nothing-from-an-existence-query-containment-is-a-predicate-not-a-fact
_A scope hides nothing from an existence query — to make a name legal only inside a region, gate the region with in_scope_kind; do not emit a fact and expect the scope to hide it_

- **answers:** I emitted a fact inside a scope and closed the scope — why does has_fact still find it | is has_fact scope-aware; which semantic-store predicates walk the active scope chain | how do I make a name legal only inside a region (a cross body, a block) in a PGEN grammar | why did SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29 use in_scope_kind instead of @emit_fact for CrossValType and CrossQueueType | why can't has_fact simply be made chain-visible (the regex grammar depends on the store-wide reading) | where do @open_scope and @close_scope bind so the scope covers the region (open-marker rule idiom) | the certificate says my new rule is UNKNOWN because the planner renders a synthetic identifier — how do I make a recognizer witnessable | the parse-cost ratchet refused my grammar fix — dispatcher first vs ordered second branch vs pre vs post predicate, which spelling is cheapest and why | why does a pre predicate on a refusal path make the packrat memo re-run everything (epoch-tainted cached failures) | how do I A/B two grammar spellings for parse cost without a release build (debug probe, protocol-graph counters, per-file entries.tsv baseline)
- **date:** 2026-09-03 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.29 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0347): the pre-registered fix (@open_scope + two @emit_fact on the cross open-marker, @close_scope on the close-marker) flipped the two fixed pins AND the invalid pin `CrossQueueType q;` after the endgroup — trace: 🔓 open ScopeId(1), 📥 both facts scope_id=ScopeId(1), 🔒 close OK, then has_fact(type_name, CrossQueueType) → true from ScopeId(0). Source: has_fact = fact_index.any_with_name, 'across the whole store … in any scope_depth'. Reproduced on a six-rule synthetic with no SystemVerilog in it (`{x}T` accepts, control `T` rejects). Routed: ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.89. Shipped: in_scope_kind(cross) as a post predicate on a terminal recognizer (a terminal, not a lookahead: the certificate planner renders a terminal from its regex and witnesses it from a cross_body union entry; post, not pre: a pre gate that reads the store on the refusal path epoch-taints the callers' cached failures — measured by the parse-cost ratchet) — the invalid pin stays REJECT, the fixed pins ACCEPT, the AST is byte-identical.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/engine_universal_services/eus89_store_wide_has_fact/probe.sh   # 2/2: the closed-scope fact is found (A1) and the gate can refuse (A2 RED control)`

### a-scope-qualifier-belongs-on-every-surface-the-prose-licenses
_A scope qualifier admitted on ONE surface (the operand) must be admitted on EVERY surface the standard's prose licenses (the call, the class scope, the handle) — and a reserved word had been hiding the missing ones_

- **answers:** local::get_x() inside randomize() with { } REJECTS on 1.0.211 while x < local::x parses — why, and what fixed it | a grammar release reserved a word and legal text stopped parsing — how do I find every surface the word was standing in for | adding A.8.4 class_qualifier's local:: to primary — which other surfaces does IEEE 1800-2017 18.7.1 license it on | which SV grammar rule carries a scoped tf-name (scoped_or_hierarchical_tf_identifier) and how does local::get_c().c1_f derive as a call chain | how do I prove a widening does not move an existing control's tree before generating (interpreter --interpret-parse-ast-json, kind multiset, byte-identity) | how was the dead block_data_type_or_implicit deleted and the syntax-closure allow-list returned to one | Annex A has no production for a text the clause prose plainly permits — annex gap or prohibition
- **date:** 2026-09-04 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.40 + .3.36 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0367, release 1.0.212, ledger SV-0085). Release 1.0.211 reserved Annex B's 248 words and gave `local ::` its A.8.4 class_qualifier production in `primary_hier_scope_prefix` — the OPERAND surface. verilator t_randomize_method_with_scoping.v:70 `doit &= f.randomize() with { get_x() == local::get_x(); };` then REJECTED (furthest_position=1337, on the `(`): the scoped trace shows `primary_hier_scope_prefix` consuming ` local::`, `primary_sv_2017` winning as a hierarchical name, and no `call_primary` alternative admitting the prefix — `tf_call`'s scoped name rule `scoped_or_hierarchical_tf_identifier` had class_scope and package_scope arms only. It had parsed on 1.0.210 only because `local` was an admissible identifier standing in for a package name. IEEE 1800-2017 18.7.1 (section-18-constrained-random-value-generation.md:1708-1726): the qualifier applies to *an identifier within an in-line constraint* and *may be used to qualify class scopes and type names*; A.8.4 reaches primary and ps_type_identifier and no tf_call production — an ANNEX GAP by the grammar's standing rule, not a prohibition. Fix: one arm `local :: [ implicit_class_handle . | class_scope ] tf_identifier` on the scoped tf-name rule; the reproducer, the corpus row, `local::get_c().c1_f`, `local::K::m()` and `local::this.f()` all parse on sv_2017 and sv_2023; the two existing controls' interpreter ASTs are BYTE-IDENTICAL; the corpus moved exactly that one row fail -> pass on both SV lanes and nothing the other way. In the same release the dead `block_data_type_or_implicit` (orphaned by .3.35's footnote-6 split) was deleted: 1576 -> 1575 rules, sv_syntax_closure_gate unreachable_rules 2 -> 1, allow-list back to [casting_type].`
- **reverify:** `python3 stimuli/sv/run_adjudication_repros.py | tail -1   # failures=0; fixed_local_scope_subroutine_call.sv ACCEPT on both SV profiles and control_local_scope_qualifier.sv unmoved; ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog --profile sv_2017 stimuli/sv/subs/verilator/test_regress/t/t_randomize_method_with_scoping.v`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-scope-qualifier-belongs-on-every-surface-the-prose-licenses.md`](docs/knowledge/a-scope-qualifier-belongs-on-every-surface-the-prose-licenses.md)

### a-search-path-entry-grants-every-name-in-it-not-the-one-it-was-derived-for
_A search-path entry grants every name in the directory, not the one it was derived for — scope a derived resolution as narrowly as its justification, and guard the names it resolves by the side door_

- **answers:** I derived an include directory for one header — what else does the preprocessor now find there | why did my context derivation start resolving an ambiguous include silently | how can a widening of what an instrument resolves create a wrong answer that no number shows | where should a resolution that is justified per file live — in the suite table or the per-file table | what guard belongs with an include-path derivation | a tie between identical copies of a header — is it ambiguous | why does pipeline_context.py refuse with exit 4
- **date:** 2026-10-06 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SVPP-EXPANSION.4d (`PGEN-SVPP-EXPANSION-0038`). The context derivation learned to resolve a tie between byte-identical copies of a header; its first cut emitted the chosen directory suite-wide. The shadow guard written in the same slice refused the real tree on the first run: OpenTitan's top_darjeeling/ip_autogen/pwrmgr/dv/env/seq_lib, chosen for pwrmgr_vseq_list.sv (4 copies, one text), also holds pwrmgr_base_vseq.sv and pwrmgr_smoke_vseq.sv (3 copies, 2 texts) — every OpenTitan includer of those two would have been handed darjeeling's copy with no number moving in the wrong direction (a refusal becoming a pass reads as progress). Redesigned: the identical tie resolves PER FILE; a per-file directory that holds an ambiguous name its includer also includes is withheld for that includer (one real case, the ip_templates pwrmgr vseq list); a suite directory in that position refuses the derivation. Before the slice the tracked table had 0 such pairs: the hazard was latent, not live, and nothing had read for it`
- **reverify:** `python3 stimuli/sv/pipeline_context.py --self-test 2>&1 | grep -E 'SHADOW|REFUSES|WITHHELD' | grep -c PASS  # expect 3: the shadow is reported, the suite form refuses (exit 4), the per-file form is withheld`

### a-separator-is-not-a-content-tail
_A whitespace separator is not a comment content tail — "has an unbounded repetition" is the wrong question, and it makes a live rule inert_

- **answers:** a rule with a '#{' or '//='-style terminal never matches and the grammar looks correct | my terminal's first character is a comment introducer — why is it eaten as trivia | the trace enters my rule at position N but attempts its first terminal at EOF | why does the layout skipper consume a token my grammar declares | when does PGEN suppress the engine's #, // or /* comment arm for a grammar | how do I tell whether a generated parser treats # as a comment | what is the blast radius of changing the comment-arm suppression predicate | how do I check which grammars claim a comment introducer as a real token | a certificate-coverage rule is UNKNOWN and its regex terminal compiles fine
- **date:** 2026-08-22 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED.H.16.2 (`PGEN-GRAMMAR-WELLFORMED-0165`). `semantic_annotation`'s `set_value := "#{" /\s*/ … "}"` could never match: `@type: #{"a", "b"}` REJECT at position 7 while the object control `@type: {"a": 1}` PASSED, on both the generated parser and `--interpret-parse`. `node_is_unbounded_content` scored the `/\s*/` separator as a comment content tail, dropping the `#` claim, so the `#`-to-EOL arm was emitted. Fix = `hir_matches_only_whitespace`. Cert `115/0/82/33 spf=2` → `115/0/84/31 spf=0`; the pinned suppression matrix moved exactly one row of ten.`
- **reverify:** `./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse semantic_annotation <(printf '@type: #{\"a\"}')   # PASS — and grep -c \"== b'#'\" generated/semantic_annotation_parser.rs  # 0, the arm is suppressed`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-separator-is-not-a-content-tail.md`](docs/knowledge/a-separator-is-not-a-content-tail.md)

_A single-character terminal that may touch its neighbour must not carry a word boundary — a closed symbol sub-language gets its own boundary-free terminals, and its rule names must not differ only by case_

### a-specialised-rule-masked-by-a-general-fallback-is-untestable-from-source
_When a GENERAL production accepts the same text as the specialised one, a defect in the specialised rule is invisible from source — enter the rule directly, then find the input the fallback cannot rescue_

- **answers:** a grammar rule looks broken but every source-level probe parses — how do I test it | how do I probe a mid-grammar rule in isolation without writing a whole source file | my census flagged candidate rules but they all seem to work — how do I confirm or clear them | is it safe to fix a rule that no source-level input reaches | how do I know whether a specialised production is reachable at all | why did a defect only appear for one particular argument shape | a fix changes no verdict on any real input — should I still land it

### a-spelling-test-standing-in-for-a-property-test
_A text census that matches how a call is SPELLED, not where its argument RESOLVES, is wrong in both directions — and it is wrong quietly_

- **answers:** my grep-based census reports far more breaches than are real — what did the classifier get wrong | how do I tell a repo-rooted mktemp template from a bare mktemp | why did my regex read a quoted argument as the end of the call | is it safe to decide a path's location from the NAME of the variable holding it | how do I stop a census classifier from silently drifting back to a spelling list | what do I pin in a census self-test so a wrong cut cannot come back | my census got cleaner after I changed the rule — is that progress or is it looking less
- **date:** 2026-09-15 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `DATA-LOCALITY.1 (2026-09-15, PGEN-DATA-LOCALITY-0001). Three successive classifiers for one question — does this call create scratch off the repository volume — were each wrong in a different way. Cut 1 matched the CALL (`\bmktemp\b(?![^\n]*-p)`) and counted every repo-rooted TEMPLATE as a breach: 52 reported, 4 real. Cut 2 required a terminator after the flags and matched the template's opening QUOTE, so `mktemp "$ROOT/…"` still read as bare. Cut 3 decided by the NAME of the variable a template used and reported three CORRECT derived-path sites. The fourth resolves a variable against its own assignments in the same file and asks where the path lands. Fourth recorded occurrence of the class in this repository: the look-around check (does the pattern COMPILE), the separator check (can it carry non-whitespace text), the comment-introducer guard (is this terminal AN introducer vs does it BEGIN with one), and this one.`
- **reverify:** `python3 scripts/data_locality_census.py --self-test   # PASS — 10 classifier arms incl. the three wrong cuts, + a REACH arm that fails if the frozen population reads zero`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-spelling-test-standing-in-for-a-property-test.md`](docs/knowledge/a-spelling-test-standing-in-for-a-property-test.md)

### a-stage-that-passes-through-what-it-did-not-resolve-lets-the-next-stage-accept-it
_A stage that passes through what it did not resolve lets the next stage accept it — a pipeline's pass is only as strong as the weakest stage's post-condition, so each stage refuses its own leftovers_

- **answers:** why does the preprocess-then-parse pipeline report pass for a file with an undefined macro | two stages are each correct on their own — how can their composition be wrong | where should an unresolved macro usage be refused: the preprocessor or the parser | why does the SystemVerilog grammar accept a bare backtick line at the top level | what is the undefined_macro_policy stage option for | how do I find rows a pipeline passes over text it never resolved
- **date:** 2026-10-06 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SVPP-EXPANSION.6f (`PGEN-SVPP-EXPANSION-0044`). The SystemVerilog preprocessor kept an undefined macro usage as written (a design the macro-string renderer and the paste walker rely on), and the SV grammar's compiler_directive rule carries the RAW lane's residue — an opaque backtick line at the top level is accepted so an unexpanded file parses around its macro uses. Composed in the pipeline, a top-level `not_defined reached the parser and the row read pass: verilator t_preproc_nodef_bad.v, sv2v error/undefined_macro.sv, and 25 riscv-dv instruction files whose macros live in a package the lane refuses — 38 passing rows over unresolved text, found by re-expanding every passing row and scanning the output for a backtick outside comments and strings; 318 failing rows carried one too. The fix is the stage's own post-condition: after expansion no backtick survives outside a comment or string unless it is a directive the parser reads — an undefined name, a function-like macro without its argument list, a stray macro-string token and an unmatched `end_keywords are refused with their clause (undefined_macro_policy=error, the default; keep restores the passthrough)`
- **reverify:** `rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_undefined_macro_usage.sv --profile sv_2017 --preprocess 2>&1 | tail -1 | grep -c 'neither a defined macro nor a compiler directive'  # expect 1: the stage refuses before the parser can accept the opaque line`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-stage-that-passes-through-what-it-did-not-resolve-lets-the-next-stage-accept-it.md`](docs/knowledge/a-stage-that-passes-through-what-it-did-not-resolve-lets-the-next-stage-accept-it.md)

### a-stale-identity-block-is-a-prompt-to-re-measure-not-evidence-of-drift
_An instrument-identity block says whether your INPUTS moved, never whether your ANSWER moved — treating a stale one as proof of drift replaces a cheap check with an expensive assumption_

- **answers:** my baseline's input hashes no longer match — do I have to re-adjudicate everything | a tracked report says it no longer describes my tree — how bad is that | how do I re-measure without confounding my change with unrelated drift | should I defer work because an oracle it depends on is stale | how do I make a delta attributable to my change by construction | when do I run the control — before or after the edit | I am moving items between two owners; what do I check first
- **date:** 2026-08-23 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13e.1 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0282). A corpus lane's tracked results oracle carried an identity block pinning generated parser bfaca030… while the tree held e53cb4a2…, and the block's own wording is `if any hash differs, this report no longer describes your tree`. That was read as: a re-run would confound three days of parser drift with the change under test, so the unit must be deferred as an atomic cascade. Measured instead: the lane re-parses in 10 s (2 459 files, peak 94 MB) and results_v2005.tsv came back BYTE-IDENTICAL — the identity was stale, the outcomes were not. Separately, re-deriving the manifest from the UNCHANGED transform before editing it produced a byte-identical file, which made every later difference attributable by construction: one transition, 147 rows, 0 rows whose observed value moved.`
- **reverify:** `python3 stimuli/sv/adjudicate_external_corpus.py --out-manifest rust/target/attr_control.tsv --out-summary rust/target/attr_control.md >/dev/null && cmp stimuli/sv/characterization/adjudication_manifest.tsv rust/target/attr_control.tsv && echo BYTE-IDENTICAL-BEFORE-CONTROL   # the pattern: re-derive from the UNCHANGED transform first`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-stale-identity-block-is-a-prompt-to-re-measure-not-evidence-of-drift.md`](docs/knowledge/a-stale-identity-block-is-a-prompt-to-re-measure-not-evidence-of-drift.md)

_How often did this artifact go stale?" is a walk over git objects, not a recollection — and a byte-stale count must be CLASSIFIED into stale-by-meaning and stale-by-spelling before it is published_

- **answers:** how often has this tracked report been stale against the thing it describes | how do I size a staleness problem over the project's whole history | the report records a digest of its input — how do I check it at every past commit | my stale count includes comment-only edits — how do I separate those | how do I show that wiring a gate actually changed behaviour, not just that it can refuse | what is the cheapest before/after measurement of a doctrine's effect

Split at the day the census gate was wired (2026-08-31): 11 stale of 31 before, 0 of 4 after.`
- **reverify:** `bash docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/outcome_staleness_census/census.sh >/dev/null && bash docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/outcome_staleness_census/classify.sh >/dev/null   # OUTCOME-STALENESS: … stale=11 stale_runs=7 ; OUTCOME-STALENESS-CLASS: … different_language=7 same_language=4`

### a-standards-own-example-text-outranks-its-annex-a-and-the-next-editions-annex-a-usually-says-so
_A standard's own example text outranks its Annex A, and the next edition's Annex A usually says so — when the LRM's example is not derivable by its formal syntax, the example is the spec and the omission is an erratum_

FIRST case SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.34 (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0362, release 1.0.209, ledger SV-0082): IEEE 1800-2017 §12.6.1 section-12-procedural-programming-statements.md:826/:828/:840 vs Annex A section-41-data-read-api.md:2279-2286 (no `( pattern )`) vs 1800-2023 section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.md:2273-2281 (`( pattern )` first); five ispras ieee-1800-2012/12/12.06.* bar rows fail -> pass on sv_2017; the .3.30 UDP-table rule's second instance`

### a-status-that-is-prose-is-a-status-nothing-checks
_A work item whose status lives in free prose can be FIXED and still read `todo` — because nothing derives the status from what the item itself recorded_

- **answers:** my tracker says a task is open but the fix already shipped — how does that happen | how do I stop a task board from over-reporting remaining work | the commit that fixed it named the ticket and the ticket still says todo | is routing a defect to another owner enough to keep the original item current | why does remaining-work always look bigger than it is | what should a status field be derived from | how do I audit whether my open items are actually still open
- **date:** 2026-08-23 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2b (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0279) and .13c.2d (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0280), found in one session. .13c.2b read `blocked on ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.13` for 9 days after ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.17 slice 9 fixed it in another tree. .13c.2d read `todo` for 6 days after its own tree's slice 3 fixed it in commit 6d1a18b3, whose subject reads verbatim `leaf SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2d fix SHIPPED`. Both statuses live as free prose inside a Markdown heading; no instrument compares that prose against the leaf's own recorded slices or against the tracked reproducer manifest, whose `class` column already reads `fixed` for both. A first-cut census was attempted and its result deliberately withheld: it matched several headings per leaf and returned 6 suspects of 11, the heading-grammar trap that DOCTRINE-GAP-OWNERSHIP.8 owns.`
- **reverify:** `grep -c 'fixed' stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/MANIFEST.tsv; git log -1 --format=%s 6d1a18b3   # the manifest already knows which defects are fixed, and the fixing commit already named its leaf — two oracles the status prose was never compared against`

- **date:** 2026-09-08 · **status:** current

CHECKER-CENSUS: lane_files=16336 with_endchecker=37 forward_instantiated=5; INSTANTIATION-HEAD-CENSUS: sv_2017 residual_rows=79 with_instantiation_head=8; FORWARD-REFERENCE-CENSUS: residual_rows=79 forward_declared_after_call_use=0.`

### a-stored-derivation-a-reader-tolerates-is-a-stored-derivation-that-drifts

### a-strictness-fix-redirects-the-search-not-just-the-predicate
_Pricing a strictness fix by asking "where does the guard execute" gets the guard exactly right and misses the larger term — rejection is not free, it buys more speculation_

- **answers:** how do I predict what a grammar tightening will cost before writing it | my parser got stricter and slower at the same time — why | why did my cost model for a lookahead come out backwards | does making a rule reject more make a backtracking parser faster or slower | how should I price a change to a memoized PEG rule | what does flat committed with rising entries tell me
- **date:** 2026-08-19 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2k (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0235). PGEN moved a reserved-word exclusion out of a wrapper rule that never takes a memo hit (5,504,191 calls / 0 hits) and into `identifier`, which is ~90% memo hits (10,349,663 calls / 9,324,559 hits). A price instrument written BEFORE the fix predicted -8,958,174 rule entries. Measured after: +7,588,879 — wrong by 16,547,053 and in the flattering direction. The attribution says why: guard evaluations fell -8,941,038, within 0.19% of prediction, while `identifier` and the wrapper were RE-ENTERED +17,820,203 more times. `committed` moved -124 on 7.1M, so ~100% of the net rise is rolled-back speculation.`
- **reverify:** `python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/raw_identifier_census/price.py   # prints the predicate-relocation term the model gets right; compare its prediction against a post-fix `total_entries` from the same instrument, and expect the difference to be re-entry, not noise`

### a-suites-intended-invalid-path-is-a-census-key-and-the-goldens-line-is-not-where-the-syntax-error-is
_A suite's intended-invalid path is a census key, and the golden's line is not where the syntax error is — re-adjudicate an answer-key class one production at a time, by parsing a twin_

- **answers:** why is a verilator _bad test keyed must_accept while PGEN rejects it — is the parser wrong or the key | the upstream golden names an error on one line but the parser stops on another — which one is the syntax error | how do I re-adjudicate a corpus answer-key row (LRM cite, measured furthest_position, two-sided control, class=invalid pin) | a construct is legal in IEEE 1800-2023 but the corpus lane judges 1800-2017 — must_reject or must_accept | the store gate rejects a name the file declares with the wrong kind (wire used as a type, package after extends, class after implements) — is that a parser defect | a probe bank went RED silently for several commits — why does a conservation law need every exit named | a control written in SV vocabulary fails under verilog_2005 — how do I scope reproducer pins per profile
- **date:** 2026-09-03 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13x.a–.13x.f (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0350 … -0356): 48 bar rows on suite-intended-invalid paths keyed must_accept — 38 BNF violations the parser was RIGHT to reject (on 9 the golden named a semantic error on a line the parser passes), 7 store-gate refusals of a wrong-kind or later-declared name (+3 the census could not see, explained by the new route 1b), 2 IEEE 1800-2023 constructs on the 1800-2017 lane, 1 parser defect (.3.31); the axis-2 bar 212 → 162 with ZERO parse verdicts moved; the .13w bank had been RED since -0347 because its conservation law forbade the `match` exit.`

- **answers:** my minimal repro reproduces the bug exactly — can I design the fix on it | how do I know a minimised grammar is still faithful when I change the question I ask it | the synthetic says rule X is the right place to fix this — does that transfer to the real grammar | is it safe to collapse a chain of bare rule references when minimising a grammar defect | why did my fix target the wrong rule even though the repro was correct

### a-token-named-after-an-annex-a-nonterminal-is-deleted-with-every-arm-that-carries-it
_A token named after an Annex A nonterminal is deleted with every arm that carries it — never gated or guarded — and the census over the whole kw_ inventory is what says it was the only one_

- **answers:** how do I find whether the grammar reserves a word that IEEE 1800 Annex B does not | why did the parser accept y = class_qualifier m; and y = null class_qualifier:=local::43; | what is kw_class_qualifier_fa08937d and why was it deleted | which kw_ tokens of the SystemVerilog grammar are not Annex B keywords | is randomize a reserved keyword in SystemVerilog | why do the sv_2017 and sv_2023 type-scope twins ps_type_identifier_scope_sv_2017 / _sv_2023 both exist | how did the grammar extractor weld a production definition line onto the previous production | when is a schema bump owed for removing a branch that no legal input ever produced
- **date:** 2026-09-23 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2m (PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0413, release 1.0.244, schema 33 -> 34): the markdown the extractor read prints `class_qualifier := [ local ::43 ] …` with ONE colon (docs/systemverilog/2023/md/section-Annex_A-normative-formal-syntax.md:3097; one such head per edition against 717 / 734 correct `::=` heads), so the head was appended to `primary`'s `null` alternative, the footnote superscript became a token and `class_qualifier` a literal keyword carried by three scope-prefix copies; nine pinned arms accepted the LRM's own production text through 1.0.243 (`accepts_invalid_*` pins, flipped to `invalid`). The census over the 318 `kw_<name>_<hash>` tokens against the three keyword annexes read line-wise from their *Reserved keywords* heading (1800-2017 = 1800-2023 = 248 names, 1364-2005 126): 248 keywords + 68 LRM literals + two residual names, `class_qualifier` (deleted) and `randomize` (A.8.4 randomize_call's own literal, not reserved; `int randomize;` parses — pinned `control_randomize_as_identifier.sv`). docs/tasks/SV-CORPUS-GRAD.md `.13c.2m`, grammars/systemverilog.ebnf `primary_hier_scope_prefix` / `ps_type_identifier_scope_sv_2017`.`
- **reverify:** `grep -c 'kw_class_qualifier\\|kw_n_43\\|kw_n_48' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf | sed 's/^/non-comment refs must be 0 among: /'; grep -nE '^kw_(class_qualifier|n_43|n_48)_' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf   # prints nothing: the three tokens are gone; then python3 stimuli/sv/run_adjudication_repros.py --verbose 2>&1 | grep -E 'accepts_invalid_class_qualifier_as_prefix|control_randomize_as_identifier'`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-token-named-after-an-annex-a-nonterminal-is-deleted-with-every-arm-that-carries-it.md`](docs/knowledge/a-token-named-after-an-annex-a-nonterminal-is-deleted-with-every-arm-that-carries-it.md)

### a-token-rule-named-after-a-keyword-silently-eats-that-keyword
_A token rule named after a keyword will silently swallow that keyword when a grammar is imported — and no coverage instrument can report it, because the keyword never becomes a rule_

- **answers:** my grammar rejects a keyword the standard defines — where do I look first | why would a parser accept an operator the standard does not define in that position | how can a defect exist that certificate coverage and corpus coverage both miss | I am importing a standard's BNF into an existing grammar — what collides | is a rule named after a keyword safe if it predates the import | what should I check before minting a keyword token that did not exist
- **date:** 2026-08-20 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2y (`PGEN-SV-CORPUS-GRAD-0261`, ledger `SV-0066`). `grammars/systemverilog.ebnf` defined `implies := trivia \"->\"` — the ARROW — years before IEEE 1800 A.2.10's property operator `implies` was extracted. Extraction resolved the keyword to the existing rule, so `a implies b` was REJECTED at every release while `-> b` and `a |= b` were ACCEPTED in property position. `grep -c kw_implies grammars/systemverilog.ebnf` returned 0 at every release. Fixed by minting `kw_implies_470cec58` and moving the operator to its Table 16-3 precedence group; union certificate `UNKNOWN` fell 53 -> 1 and the generated parser shed 8.41 MB, because the mis-encoded alternative was also the only left-recursive one in its rule.`
- **reverify:** `printf 'kw_implies present: %s\\nthe rule named implies is: %s\\n' \"$(grep -c kw_implies grammars/systemverilog.ebnf)\" \"$(grep -m1 '^implies :=' grammars/systemverilog.ebnf)\"`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-token-rule-named-after-a-keyword-silently-eats-that-keyword.md`](docs/knowledge/a-token-rule-named-after-a-keyword-silently-eats-that-keyword.md)

### a-token-the-standard-writes-contiguously-must-be-one-terminal
_A token the STANDARD writes contiguously must be ONE terminal — composing it out of grammar elements silently accepts the spaced spelling, because layout is skipped between elements_

- **answers:** the LRM writes this token with no spaces — do I model it as a sequence or as one regex | how do I stop my grammar accepting a whitespace-separated version of a fused token | my repair for a mis-transcribed terminal would over-accept — what is the shape that does not | when is a follow-restriction / lexical annotation actually needed and when is it not | the identifier grammar admits $ or . inside a name — what does that mean for a token containing one | how do I decide between a scannerless composition and a single terminal regex
- **date:** 2026-08-17 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2f slice 4. IEEE 1800 A.7.5 writes `PATHPULSE$specify_input_terminal_descriptor$specify_output_terminal_descriptor`; the LRM→EBNF extraction transliterated the `$` into the word `_dollar` and flattened both nonterminal references into the token text, so `pulse_control_specparam` was unreachable through BOTH alternatives and IEEE 1800-2023 §30.7.1's own example REJECTED at `furthest_position=166`. The planned repair was the composed form (`PATHPULSE$` descriptor `$` descriptor) plus a `[> … ]` follow restriction to stop it spanning whitespace; the composed form was never built, because `trivia` skips layout before every element and A.9.3 makes `PATHPULSE$clk$q` ONE simple identifier — so `PATHPULSE$ clk $ q` is three tokens and is not legal. One contiguous regex refuses it BY CONSTRUCTION. Measured after the fix - `PATHPULSE$ clk $ q = (2, 9);` REJECT, `PATHPULSE$clk$q = (2, 9);` ACCEPT, corpus 16 336 files with 3 rows improving and 0 regressing, accepts-invalid unchanged at 21.`
- **reverify:** `python3 stimuli/sv/run_adjudication_repros.py 2>&1 | tail -1   # invalid_pathpulse_spaced_descriptors.sv must stay REJECT; failures=0`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-token-the-standard-writes-contiguously-must-be-one-terminal.md`](docs/knowledge/a-token-the-standard-writes-contiguously-must-be-one-terminal.md)

### a-tolerated-construct-owes-its-syntax-box-and-a-key-can-be-right-about-the-form-and-wrong-about-the-stage
_A construct the parser TOLERATES owes the clause its syntax box (tolerance without the box's syntax is over-acceptance, and "not in Annex A" is where such boxes hide), an answer key can be right about the FORM of a defect and wrong about its STAGE, and a corpus census's file list is a text selection whose misses the parser must name_

- **answers:** the parser tolerates `timescale / `pragma / `line lines as opaque text — is `timescale frump an over-acceptance | which IEEE 1800 syntax boxes are captioned 'not in Annex A' and does the grammar transcribe them | how are compiler directives typed in the SystemVerilog AST since 1.0.217 — what does body carry | is the magnitude of a `timescale argument syntax or a value rule — 1, 10, 100 — and why does timeunit 2ps still parse | sv2v line_char1 / t_pp_line_bad were keyed preprocessing-stage — why are they must_reject now | a suite tags a directive-argument error ':type: preprocessing' or 'simulation elaboration' — does the tag decide the key | `begin_keywords \"1800-2023\" — legal under sv_2017 or only under sv_2023 | `begin_keywords \"VAMS-2.3\" — which lane owns a Verilog-AMS file, and does the parser refuse the directive | a parse stops ON `default_nettype inside a `define continuation line — is that svpp-explained | a parse stops ON `timescale whose arguments are macro uses — svpp-explained or unexplained | the census file list selected a file by grep but the parser read no directive node in it — what is no_node | how do I census every compiler-directive line the corpus writes and classify it against clause 22 (DIRECTIVE-CLASSIFY) | what is the residue the parser still tolerates as an opaque backtick line, and under which profile is `undefineall opaque
- **date:** 2026-09-06 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.39 (release 1.0.217, ledger SV-0090, schema 28 -> 29). IEEE 1800-2017 clause 22 gives thirteen directives a syntax box, every one captioned 'not in Annex A' (docs/systemverilog/2017/md/section-22-compiler-directives.md 22.3 :72-86, 22.5.2 :395-407, 22.5.3 :408-412, 22.7 :615-633, 22.8 :681-686, 22.9 :693-716, 22.10 :717-726, 22.11 :734-763, 22.12 :804-822, 22.14 :851-870); through 1.0.216 compiler_directive := trivia /`[^\\r\\n]*/ carried each as one string. The census (AST-FIELD-CENSUS kind=compiler_directive field=body over the 699 lane files carrying a typed-name line; classify.py DIRECTIVE-CLASSIFY) read 1 615 typed lines on sv_2017: legal=1552 ILLEGAL=51 TRAILING=10 opaque=146 macro_body=2 no_node=1, the 51 illegal in 26 accepting files — every one a box refusal — and 0 on verilog_2005. Keys corrected on the FORM/STAGE distinction: sv2v line_char1/line_char2/line_eof/line_level (pinned .8b.2 'directive-argument validity, preprocessing stage') and default_nettype_invalid (SV2V_PREPROC), sv-tests 22.12--line-illegal-1..5 and 22.11--pragma-invalid (':type: preprocessing'), 22.9--unconnected_drive-invalid-1..3 and 22.7--timescale-basic-3 (':type: simulation elaboration'), verilator t_pp_defnettype_bad / t_pp_line_bad / t_pp_pragma_bad (the t_pp_* rule) -> must_reject with the clause; iverilog begin_keywords_1800_2023.v -> must_reject on the 2017 lane as an EDITION CONTRAST (must_accept on the 2023 lane); six Verilog-AMS files -> out_of_scope_with_cause:verilog_ams_lane by a suite-neutral rule (every `begin_keywords in the file names a VAMS version; the mixed keyword-region test t_preproc_kwd.v is not taken). Two adjudicator refinements, each with RED/GREEN arms: a stop on a `define CONTINUATION line is svpp-explained (sv2v test/core/default_nettype.sv), and a stop ON a pass-through directive is explained exactly when an ARGUMENT is a text-macro use (verilator t_time_vpi.v `timescale `time_scale_units / `time_scale_prec). The no_node row: Surelog tests/BeginKeywords/top.v, whose two directives sit inside a block comment.`
- **reverify:** `python3 docs/tasks/artifacts/sv_corpus_grad/directive_census/classify.py --self-test | tail -1   # misses=0; ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/invalid_directive_timescale_bad_unit.sv --profile sv_2017; echo rc=$?   # rc 1 since 1.0.217; ./rust/target/release/parseability_probe --parse systemverilog stimuli/sv/adjudication_repros/control_directive_begin_keywords_2023.sv --profile sv_2023; echo rc=$?   # rc 0 (and rc 1 under sv_2017); python3 -c \"import importlib.util as u; s=u.spec_from_file_location('a','stimuli/sv/adjudicate_external_corpus.py'); m=u.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); m._self_check_arm_split(); print('arms ok')\"`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-tolerated-construct-owes-its-syntax-box-and-a-key-can-be-right-about-the-form-and-wrong-about-the-stage.md`](docs/knowledge/a-tolerated-construct-owes-its-syntax-box-and-a-key-can-be-right-about-the-form-and-wrong-about-the-stage.md)

### a-transparent-rule-inherits-the-greed-of-the-rule-it-forwards-to
_A rule whose alternative is a BARE reference inherits that rule's greed — so a starvation check on direct holders alone misses the holder one hop out_

- **answers:** left-recursion elimination made an unrelated construct stop parsing — why | how do I tell whether a rule is safe to rewrite into base ( suffix )* | my starvation analysis says the base rule is safe and a neighbouring rule regressed | why does 8'(1) parse in a constant expression but not in a statement after LR elimination | what does a bare-reference alternative propagate besides the AST | is checking direct holders of the base rule enough before eliminating left recursion

### a-two-lifecycle-file-needs-a-guard-at-the-boundary
_One path holding two lifecycles — a part meant to be overwritten and a part that must never be — loses the second part, and if the workflow RESTORES the path the loss is invisible to every commit-time gate_

- **answers:** how do I stop a template's header being destroyed when someone fills in the body | a fixture file has a documented header and a throwaway body — how do I protect the header | my gate cannot see the damage because the workflow reverts the file before committing | where should a guard run when the failure never reaches a commit | is adding a do-not-edit comment enough to protect part of a file | how do I let a document be reworded but not destroyed | should a guard that refuses also offer to repair
- **date:** 2026-08-15 · **status:** current
- **evidence:** `PARSE-HARNESS.11. PGEN's blessed scratch slot `grammars/scratch/scratch.ebnf` is one tracked path holding a 32-line operating manual and a body documented as free to overwrite. An agent loading a probe grammar replaced the whole file. All 19 registered doctrines stayed GREEN over the destroyed manual, the scratch integration test passed (it asserts the BODY parses), and `git diff --quiet` on that path exited 0 after the normal restore — so no commit-time gate could ever have seen it. Closed by a two-tier check whose `--probe-time` tier hangs off the make rule that depends on the file, i.e. it runs exactly when the file has changed.`
- **reverify:** `bash scripts/check_scratch_slot_header.sh --self-test   # 8 passed, 0 failed — including the incident reproduced exactly, a single missing anchor, and a proof the repair preserves the probe body`
- **source:** [`docs/knowledge/a-two-lifecycle-file-needs-a-guard-at-the-boundary.md`](docs/knowledge/a-two-lifecycle-file-needs-a-guard-at-the-boundary.md)

### a-type-reference-comparison-is-legal-exactly-where-a-constant-expression-is-required
_A SystemVerilog type-reference comparison `type(a) == type(b)` is legal exactly where a constant_expression is required — Annex A of both editions puts type_reference in constant_primary and in no primary — and a leaf opened on "not a corpus row" owes a grep on the construct's own token before it is worked_

- **answers:** why does PGEN reject if (type(a) == type(b)) inside an initial block while generate if (type(a) == type(b)) parses | is a procedural case (type(x)) with type(...) items legal SystemVerilog | where may the SystemVerilog type operator appear in an expression — constant_primary, casting_type, data_type | what does IEEE 1800-2017 footnote 40 / 1800-2023 footnote 45 restrict about type_reference | why is sv-tests chapter-6/6.23--type_op_compare.sv keyed must_reject | why are verilator t_type_compare.v and t_type_expression_compare.v keyed must_reject | how was the SV-CORPUS-GRAD.3.32 partition question ruled and on what evidence | what does the parser stop on when it meets type(a) == type(b) in procedural code — the static cast's apostrophe | why did the .3.32 leaf say not a corpus row when three bar rows carried the construct | how does production_parity.py treat a wrongly cited Annex A line range — it compares the enclosing production faithfully
